a199.speaker: Cyril Ramaphosa, President of South Africa
a199.name: Cyril Ramaphosa
a199.title: President of South Africa
a199.speech: Rejected on Monday the accusations of his American counterpart Donald Trump according to which South Africa is "confiscating" land following the promulgation of an expropriation law. "The South African government has not confiscated any land," Mr Ramaphosa stated in a communiqué ; "The recently adopted expropriation law is not an instrument of confiscation. It is a legal procedure that guarantees access to land in a just and equitable manner, in accordance with the Constitution" ; "We look forward to discussing our land reform policy and other issues with the Trump administration," he added, hoping that following these exchanges the two countries would have a "better common understanding."

a199.speaker: Donald Trump, President of the United States (Truth Social post)
a199.name: Donald Trump
a199.title: President of the United States (Truth Social post)
a199.speech: "South Africa is confiscating land and treating certain classes of people VERY BADLY," Donald Trump wrote on his Truth Social network. "I will cut all future funding to South Africa until a full investigation of this situation has been completed!"

a199.speaker: Cyril Ramaphosa, President of South Africa
a199.name: Cyril Ramaphosa
a199.title: President of South Africa
a199.speech: Regarding the threat to suspend American aid, specified that apart from aid coming from the American Pepfar programme to fight HIV/AIDS, "there is no other significant funding from the United States to South Africa" ; "The United States remains a strategic political and trade partner for South Africa," he nevertheless stressed.

a199.speaker: Pretoria (South African government)
a199.name: Pretoria (South African government)
a199.speech: Maintains that the text does not allow the authorities to carry out expropriations arbitrarily, and that they must first attempt to reach an agreement with the owner.

a199.speaker: Certain critics of the law
a199.name: Certain critics of the law
a199.speech: Say they fear a situation similar to what neighbouring Zimbabwe experienced after its independence, when in the early 2000s some 4,000 of the then 4,500 large white landowners were forcibly expelled from their land in favour of black farmers on the orders of Robert Mugabe's government.

a251.speaker: Ban Ki-moon, then United Nations Secretary-General
a251.name: Ban Ki-moon
a251.title: then United Nations Secretary-General
a251.speech: "You know, Luc, when I was a child, my country, South Korea, was extremely poor, ravaged by war. At that time, Ghana was among the countries that had sent us humanitarian aid. Ghana then had a better economic scorecard than Korea. What has happened since? And in your view, what must change?"

a251.speaker: Ngugi wa Thiong'o, writer (quoted)
a251.name: Ngugi wa Thiong'o
a251.title: writer (quoted)
a251.speech: "The decolonisation of the mind is the precondition of any true decolonisation."

a298.speaker: Tom Fletcher, UN Under-Secretary-General for Humanitarian Affairs and Emergency Relief Coordinator
a298.name: Tom Fletcher
a298.title: UN Under-Secretary-General for Humanitarian Affairs and Emergency Relief Coordinator
a298.speech: "For countries affected by conflict, climate change and economic shocks, a drastic reduction in funding does not mean that humanitarian needs will disappear. The current allocation from the emergency fund makes it possible to channel resources quickly to where they are most needed."

a352.speaker: Reporters Without Borders (RSF) (press release)
a352.name: Reporters Without Borders (RSF) (press release)
a352.speech: In a publication made public, deplores the suspension of American international aid by Donald Trump, a situation which it says is plunging global journalism into chaos; denouncing a decision that plunges NGOs, media outlets and journalists doing essential work into the chaos of uncertainty, RSF calls on international public and private supporters to commit to the sustainability of independent media.

a352.speaker: Marco Rubio, United States Secretary of State
a352.name: Marco Rubio
a352.title: United States Secretary of State
a352.speech: On Monday 3 February declared that he was taking the role of acting head of USAID, confirming the intention expressed by Donald Trump and Elon Musk to transfer the agency under the authority of the State Department.

a352.speaker: Elon Musk, head of the quasi-official Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE)
a352.name: Elon Musk
a352.title: head of the quasi-official Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE)
a352.speech: The South African billionaire had even expressed the wish to see USAID "close completely", calling it "a criminal organisation".

a352.speaker: Clayton Weimers, Director of RSF's North America bureau
a352.name: Clayton Weimers
a352.title: Director of RSF's North America bureau
a352.speech: "The freezing of American aid funding is sowing chaos throughout the world, including in journalism. The programmes that have been frozen provide vital support to projects that strengthen the media, transparency and democracy. President Trump justified this executive order by accusing - without evidence - a so-called 'foreign aid industry' of not being aligned with American interests. The tragic irony is that this measure will create a vacuum that could play into the hands of propagandists and authoritarian states. Reporters Without Borders (RSF) is issuing an international appeal to public and private funders to commit to ensuring the sustainability of independent media."

a352.speaker: USAID 2023 data
a352.name: USAID 2023 data
a352.speech: According to USAID data from 2023, the agency funded the training of and supported 6,200 journalists, assisted 707 non-state media outlets and supported 279 civil society organisations working to strengthen independent media.

a352.speaker: A Belarusian exiled media outlet (anonymous)
a352.name: A Belarusian exiled media outlet (anonymous)
a352.speech: "We have articles planned until the end of January, but after that, if we have not found solutions, we will no longer be able to publish," explains a Belarusian media outlet in exile that wished to remain anonymous.

a352.speaker: An Iranian exiled media outlet (anonymous)
a352.name: An Iranian exiled media outlet (anonymous)
a352.speech: Had to suspend its collaboration with its team for three months and reduce salaries to the bare minimum in an attempt to survive.

a352.speaker: A woman journalist interviewed by RSF (anonymous)
a352.name: A woman journalist interviewed by RSF (anonymous)
a352.speech: Warns that the impact of this funding freeze could silence some of the last free voices, creating a vacuum that Iranian state propaganda would inevitably fill: "Silencing us means giving them more power," she denounces.

a352.speaker: Anna Babinets, director and co-founder of Slidstvo.Info (Kyiv-based independent investigative outlet)
a352.name: Anna Babinets
a352.title: director and co-founder of Slidstvo.Info (Kyiv-based independent investigative outlet)
a352.speech: "At Slidstvo.Info, 80% of our budget is affected."

a352.speaker: Anna Babinets, director and co-founder of Slidstvo.Info
a352.name: Anna Babinets
a352.title: director and co-founder of Slidstvo.Info
a352.speech: "Some media outlets could close or be bought by businessmen or oligarchs. I think Russian money will enter the market. And government propaganda, of course, will intensify," she comments.

a352.speaker: Oleh Dereniuha, editor-in-chief of the Ukrainian local media outlet NikVesti (Mykolaiv)
a352.name: Oleh Dereniuha
a352.title: editor-in-chief of the Ukrainian local media outlet NikVesti (Mykolaiv)
a352.speech: "The suspension of American funding is only the tip of the iceberg - a key case that illustrates the seriousness of the situation."

a352.speaker: RSF report
a352.name: RSF report
a352.speech: A recent RSF report underlines the need to focus on the economic recovery of Ukrainian independent media, weakened by the full-scale Russian invasion of 24 February 2022, which RSF estimates at at least $96 million over three years.

a352.speaker: Prime Minister of Georgia
a352.name: Prime Minister of Georgia
a352.speech: Welcomed the American president's decision, at a time when Georgia's law on the transparency of foreign influence - modelled on Russian legislation - is endangering many media organisations.

a352.speaker: United States government
a352.name: United States government
a352.speech: Officially, this suspension is only supposed to last 90 days, according to the American government.

a352.speaker: Katerina Abramova, communications director of the exiled media outlet Meduza
a352.name: Katerina Abramova
a352.title: communications director of the exiled media outlet Meduza
a352.speech: Fears that the review of funding contracts will take much longer: "Media in exile are even more vulnerable than others, because we cannot monetise our audience and crowdfunding has its limits - especially when making a donation to Meduza is a crime in Russia," she stresses.

a365.speaker: European Court of Human Rights (ruling)
a365.name: European Court of Human Rights (ruling)
a365.speech: Ruled that Russia violated international law in Ukraine, marking the first time an international court has found Moscow responsible for human rights abuses since the full-scale invasion in 2022; judges also ruled on Wednesday that Russia was behind the downing of Malaysia Airlines Flight 17 (MH17), the first time Moscow was named by an international court as being responsible for the 2014 tragedy that killed 298 people.

a365.speaker: United Nations' aviation agency (ICAO)
a365.name: United Nations' aviation agency (ICAO)
a365.speech: Found Russia responsible for the MH17 disaster in May.

a365.speaker: Ukraine (government)
a365.name: Ukraine (government)
a365.speech: Said on Wednesday that eight civilians were killed in Russian drone and bombing attacks in the Donetsk region — five in the town of Rodynske and three in the town of Kostiantynivka.

a365.speaker: Families of the victims of the MH17 disaster
a365.name: Families of the victims of the MH17 disaster
a365.speech: See the decision as an important milestone in their 11-year quest for justice.

a471.speaker: Gaboyo Bakwena, secretary general of the BDFRMA (Botswana Defence Force Retired Members Association)
a471.name: Gaboyo Bakwena
a471.title: secretary general of the BDFRMA (Botswana Defence Force Retired Members Association)
a471.speech: In an interview at the retired soldiers’ Annual General Meeting in Palapye last Saturday, said military experience would give Shorland the competitive edge over its peers.

a556.speaker: Othman Masoud Othman, Zanzibar presidential candidate for ACT Wazalendo and First Vice-President of Zanzibar
a556.name: Othman Masoud Othman
a556.title: Zanzibar presidential candidate for ACT Wazalendo and First Vice-President of Zanzibar
a556.speech: Promised to deal comprehensively with the challenges of sexual abuse and gender-based violence against women and children on the islands; said Zanzibar cannot be a place that tolerates wrongdoers and stressed that the law must take its course without favouritism. "The government I will lead will take firm measures to combat such acts in order to protect the rights of women and children" ; "Zanzibar has been known as an island nation that follows religious principles, but at present the situation has changed because of the increase in baseless things in society" ; said it is the duty of religious leaders, parents and teachers to cooperate in returning society to good morals and principles of respect ; promised to establish special councils on morals and community safety in every district to deal swiftly with gender-based violence cases and provide legal assistance to victims, and stressed that the fight against violence cannot succeed without the cooperation of the whole society, so an ACT government will ensure preventive education and child protection are provided in schools and religious institutions.

a556.speaker: Othman Masoud Othman, Zanzibar presidential candidate for ACT Wazalendo
a556.name: Othman Masoud Othman
a556.title: Zanzibar presidential candidate for ACT Wazalendo
a556.speech: Gave the example that the lack of employment for young women is another form of systemic abuse that is forgotten and not given the weight it deserves; explained that this challenge puts many young women in risky environments, which can contribute to harassment. "I will fully address the issue of employment and economic opportunities for all young people, especially for women, by ensuring every young person has the chance to be self-employed or to get a dignified job" ; promised that an ACT government would create a friendly environment for entrepreneurship, technical training and small loans to reduce the dependency that fuels gender-based abuse.

a556.speaker: Religious leaders (imams, madrasa teachers and sheikhs of Pemba)
a556.name: Religious leaders (imams
a556.title: madrasa teachers and sheikhs of Pemba)
a556.speech: Told Othman of their sorrow over the increase in acts of violence against children, something that is eroding respect for moral values.

a556.speaker: Sheikh Ali Juma Hamad, resident of Wingwi
a556.name: Sheikh Ali Juma Hamad
a556.title: resident of Wingwi
a556.speech: Said that at present the issue of abuse of women and children in Zanzibari society has become a disgrace: "You can hear of a 70-year-old man having sex with a five-year-old child; people, this is where we have reached, brother candidate (Othman); we are losing the workforce of the future."

a556.speaker: Kombo Khamis Kombo, religious leader
a556.name: Kombo Khamis Kombo
a556.title: religious leader
a556.speech: Emphasised the matter, saying it is the right time to put an end to acts of abuse and to enact laws that will remove that challenge from the islands.

a556.speaker: Zanzibar Gender-Based Violence and Abuse Statistics (report)
a556.name: Zanzibar Gender-Based Violence and Abuse Statistics (report)
a556.speech: State that a total of 97 incidents of gender-based violence and abuse were reported in June 2025; of those incidents most of the victims were children, at 85.6 percent, followed by women at 12.4 percent and men at 2.1 percent.

a608.speaker: Confederation of Zimbabwe Industries (CZI)
a608.name: Confederation of Zimbabwe Industries (CZI)
a608.speech: Says the manufacturing sector's negative performance reflects a gap between government policy measures and set National Development Strategy 1 goals.

a608.speaker: Kurai Matsheza, CZI president
a608.name: Kurai Matsheza
a608.title: CZI president
a608.speech: Told the organisation's annual congress last week that the downward trend in the manufacturing sector was worrying as it implied de-industrialisation.

a624.speaker: Article in the medical journal "The Lancet" (study)
a624.name: Article in the medical journal "The Lancet" (study)
a624.speech: Says the onslaught by the Trump regime against USAID could lead to 14 million deaths in developing countries by 2030 ; warned that the destruction of USAID could halt, and even throw into reverse, "two decades of progress in health among vulnerable populations".

a624.speaker: International team of researchers (study co-authors)
a624.name: International team of researchers (study co-authors)
a624.speech: Looking back over data from 133 nations, estimated that USAID funding had prevented 91 million deaths in developing countries between 2001 and 2021, and used modelling to project how funding being slashed by 83 percent could affect death rates, finding the cuts could lead to more than 14 million avoidable deaths by 2030, including over 4.5 million children under the age of five ; found that programmes supported by USAID were linked to a 15-percent decrease in deaths from all causes, twice as steep at 32 percent for children under five, with 65 per cent fewer deaths from HIV/AIDS in countries receiving a high level of support and deaths from malaria similarly cut in half.

a624.speaker: Elon Musk, billionaire and then close ally of Donald Trump
a624.name: Elon Musk
a624.title: billionaire and then close ally of Donald Trump
a624.speech: Boasted gleefully of having put the Agency "through the woodchipper".

a624.speaker: Davide Rasella, researcher at the Barcelona Institute for Global Health (ISGlobal) and study co-author
a624.name: Davide Rasella
a624.title: researcher at the Barcelona Institute for Global Health (ISGlobal) and study co-author
a624.speech: Warned that, for many low- and middle-income countries, the shock from dismantling USAID "would be comparable in scale to a global pandemic or a major armed conflict."

a624.speaker: James Macinko, University of California, Los Angeles, study co-author
a624.name: James Macinko
a624.title: University of California, Los Angeles, study co-author
a624.speech: "US citizens contribute about 17 cents per day to USAID, around 64 dollars per year." ; "I think most people would support continued USAID funding if they knew just how effective such a small contribution can be to saving millions of lives."

a650.speaker: Dr Aspect Maunganidze, Health and Child Care permanent secretary (Zimbabwe)
a650.name: Dr Aspect Maunganidze
a650.title: Health and Child Care permanent secretary (Zimbabwe)
a650.speech: confirmed that Zimbabwe is crafting a new HIV sustainability strategy to counteract the impacts of the withdrawal of support by development partners following a United States policy shift, and said the country is proactively working to mitigate the impact of lost funding triggered by an Executive Order from US President Donald Trump restricting foreign aid: “Our health delivery system has been affected by the abrupt cessation of funding from some of our foreign partners.” ; “I am glad that the move by the United States Government came when we were already engaged in processes to develop an HIV sustainability plan, which will be ready for implementation soon.” ; said his Ministry has already taken steps to ensure that people are not severely affected, especially those taking antiretroviral therapy, including increasing the budgetary allocation, budget reprioritization, introducing the National Health Insurance Scheme, and other measures.

a650.speaker: Dr Aspect Maunganidze, Health and Child Care permanent secretary (Zimbabwe)
a650.name: Dr Aspect Maunganidze
a650.title: Health and Child Care permanent secretary (Zimbabwe)
a650.speech: “Your role as the media in this regard will be very crucial as the nation grapples with the mentioned funding gaps, the discussions and decisions we need to take to ensure that our response is sustainable and meets the expectations of our people without leaving anyone behind.” ; “Your power is not just in informing and educating but in setting the national policy agenda, reframing narratives, and advocating for the health and social transformation envisioned by the Second Republic.”

a650.speaker: Dr Owen Mgurungi, Director of the AIDS and TB Unit, Ministry of Health and Child Care (Zimbabwe)
a650.name: Dr Owen Mgurungi
a650.title: Director of the AIDS and TB Unit, Ministry of Health and Child Care (Zimbabwe)
a650.speech: weighed in, saying Zimbabwe’s aim to become an upper-middle-income economy by 2025 means the country should not rely much on aid: “We were already on the right path because upper-middle-income economies do not rely much on external funding. We need to mobilize more resources so that we do not reverse the gains we have made.”

a726.speaker: Michele Bachmann and Rick Perry, Republican presidential candidates
a726.name: Michele Bachmann and Rick Perry
a726.title: Republican presidential candidates

a726.speaker: Ron Paul and Jon Huntsman, Republican presidential candidates
a726.name: Ron Paul and Jon Huntsman
a726.title: Republican presidential candidates
a726.speech: Refused to endorse such methods, calling them what they are: torture; kept offering the rhetorical equivalent of “Whoa there, big guys, wait a minute, you’re advocating yet another war in the Middle East and South Asia” from the left- and libertarian-wings of their party.

a726.speaker: Mitt Romney, Republican presidential candidate
a726.name: Mitt Romney
a726.title: Republican presidential candidate
a726.speech: In an exercise of pure dog-whistle politicking, stared at the crowd (and a national television audience) to say he was calling this election a referendum on whether or not Obama should be allowed to permit Iran’s acquisition of nukes.

a726.speaker: Rick Perry, Republican presidential candidate
a726.name: Rick Perry
a726.title: Republican presidential candidate
a726.speech: Offered as his solution to most foreign policy questions cutting foreign assistance to those ungrateful foreigners.

a726.speaker: Barack Obama, U.S. President
a726.name: Barack Obama
a726.title: U.S. President
a726.speech: As Obama said to reporters, “I am confident we can get this done” (on the Trans-Pacific Partnership trade pact); he also spoke at a business leaders’ forum from corporations involved in trans-Pacific trade and investment, publicly pushing China to participate in new trade-opening initiatives.

a726.speaker: Hu Jintao, Chinese President
a726.name: Hu Jintao
a726.title: Chinese President
a726.speech: Just before the APEC meeting convened, restated his nation’s commitment to APEC’s long-term goal of a Free Trade Area of the Asia Pacific region.

a923.speaker: Marco Rubio, US Secretary of State
a923.name: Marco Rubio
a923.title: US Secretary of State
a923.speech: In March, announced that the Trump administration had cancelled more than 80 per cent of all the USAID programmes.

a923.speaker: Oxfam International (global advocacy group)
a923.name: Oxfam International (global advocacy group)
a923.speech: Saying the cuts to development aid were the largest since 1960.

a923.speaker: United Nations
a923.name: United Nations
a923.speech: Puts the growing gap in annual development finance at $4 trillion.

a923.speaker: FfD4 Conference organisers
a923.name: FfD4 Conference organisers
a923.speech: Have said the key focus of the talks is restructuring finance for the 17 UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) adopted at the last meeting in 2015 and expected to be met by 2030.

a923.speaker: Chola Milambo, Zambia’s permanent representative to the UN
a923.name: Chola Milambo
a923.title: Zambia’s permanent representative to the UN
a923.speech: Said the document shows that the world can tackle the financial challenges in the way of achieving the development goals, “and that multilateralism can still work”.

a923.speaker: Oxfam International
a923.name: Oxfam International
a923.speech: Has condemned the document for lacking ambition and said “the interests of a very wealthy are put over those of everyone else”.

a1145.speaker: Neal Rijkenberg, Minister of Finance of Eswatini
a1145.name: Neal Rijkenberg
a1145.title: Minister of Finance of Eswatini
a1145.speech: Has urged for innovative approaches to teaching integrated farming, suggesting starting with a few crops first and incorporating livestock. He emphasized minimal ploughing and very low fertilizer usage, encouraging farmers to integrate livestock for manure production. "Integration means having compost and manures, like the East is doing, whether using animal waste from goats, cows, or chickens for the manure."

a1145.speaker: Neal Rijkenberg, Minister of Finance of Eswatini
a1145.name: Neal Rijkenberg
a1145.title: Minister of Finance of Eswatini
a1145.speech: With Africa's population rising and land holdings shrinking, stressed the need for strategic small-scale agriculture. "Less than half of agriculture land on SNL is cultivated every year which has potential. How do you make a one-hectare piece of land commercial and have a farmer manage it all year round?" he questioned. He noted that Eswatini had adopted a Western commercial approach, while Eastern countries had successfully cracked integrated farming.

a1145.speaker: Neal Rijkenberg, Minister of Finance of Eswatini
a1145.name: Neal Rijkenberg
a1145.title: Minister of Finance of Eswatini
a1145.speech: Proposed that 100,000 homesteads participate in a tree-planting scheme, with each homestead planting 20 trees, creating a large-scale, small-farmer-driven project. The minister highlighted the need for public-private partnerships (PPPs) to provide ready financing or credit guarantee schemes for farmers.

a1145.speaker: Neal Rijkenberg, Minister of Finance of Eswatini
a1145.name: Neal Rijkenberg
a1145.title: Minister of Finance of Eswatini
a1145.speech: "We need a fund of over E1 billion so that when that farmer needs finance, we provide it—whether to buy seeds, farming inputs, or sows." He emphasized involving financial institutions, agro-processors, exporters, and the supply chain, ensuring farmers have guaranteed markets, including for pork processing and potential exports. "So when we start producing more pork than the country can use, we are ready to export."

a1217.speaker: Olushegun Adjadi Bakari, Minister of Foreign Affairs of Benin
a1217.name: Olushegun Adjadi Bakari
a1217.title: Minister of Foreign Affairs of Benin
a1217.speech: "The objective is to be able to use the actions we carry out to attract more investment, mobilise more resources and, in general, intensify our country's international influence," he maintained, speaking to the Presidency's Communication Department ; "Today, when Benin is spoken of on the international stage, the words that come to mind are rigour, industrial country, good governance, country of entrepreneurs, a country in which a certain number of challenges have been successfully met…" ; The ultimate aim, he specified, is to ensure that every Beninese is proud of their country.

a1286.speaker: Qatar, Egypt and the United States
a1286.name: Qatar
a1286.title: Egypt and the United States
a1286.speech: called on Hamas and Israel to finalise an agreement that embodies the principles outlined by US President Joe Biden on May 31, 2024.

a1286.speaker: World Health Organization (WHO)
a1286.name: World Health Organization (WHO)
a1286.speech: said there are almost no health services remaining in Rafah after the city's last partially functioning hospital, the al-Helal al-Emirati Hospital, shut down amid the ongoing hostilities.

a1286.speaker: Thousands of Israeli protesters
a1286.name: Thousands of Israeli protesters
a1286.speech: took to the streets urging Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to strike a deal with Hamas and free the captives held in Gaza.

a1286.speaker: Far-right ministers in the Israeli government
a1286.name: Far-right ministers in the Israeli government
a1286.speech: threatened to topple his government if he accepts such an agreement.

a1401.speaker: Julien Matter, new Head of Mission of Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) in Guinea (on MSF's origins and principles)
a1401.name: Julien Matter
a1401.title: new Head of Mission of Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) in Guinea (on MSF's origins and principles)
a1401.speech: Recalled the origins of MSF, created 50 years ago by journalists and doctors, and that the organisation rests on a fundamental principle: testimony. "The doctor treats, but the journalist can make the situation change," he explained. He also evoked the constant challenges encountered by MSF, such as obstacles to humanitarian aid, citing notably the current situation in Gaza and in other parts of the world. He answered journalists' questions on the challenges linked to humanitarian access in certain rural areas of the country, as well as the management of recurrent epidemics such as measles.

a1401.speaker: Julien Matter, Head of Mission of MSF in Guinea (on MSF's historical role in Guinea)
a1401.name: Julien Matter
a1401.title: Head of Mission of MSF in Guinea (on MSF's historical role in Guinea)
a1401.speech: Indicated that his organisation played a crucial role in humanitarian assistance to refugees fleeing the civil wars in Liberia and Sierra Leone between 1990 and 2000, by building and managing camps in Nzérékoré, Guéckédou, Forécariah and Macenta, and that the organisation also put in place durable solutions for drinking water and sanitation in those camps.

a1401.speaker: Julien Matter, Head of Mission of MSF in Guinea (on HIV/AIDS work in Conakry)
a1401.name: Julien Matter
a1401.title: Head of Mission of MSF in Guinea (on HIV/AIDS work in Conakry)
a1401.speech: Evoked the introduction of new diagnostic techniques and the continuous training of local doctors and nurses. He underlined the operational research efforts, notably on viral resistance, and insisted on the importance of free care and testing.

a1401.speaker: Julien Matter, Head of Mission of MSF in Guinea (on epidemic response and the Kouroussa malaria project)
a1401.name: Julien Matter
a1401.title: Head of Mission of MSF in Guinea (on epidemic response and the Kouroussa malaria project)
a1401.speech: Stated that MSF works closely with the Ministry of Health and the National Health Security Agency (ANSS) to strengthen local capacities for epidemic management. He underlined the importance of continuous training of health professionals and the integration of operational research, particularly with the deployment of new services such as palliative care. He described the Kouroussa malaria project as an illustration of MSF's commitment to long-term public health interventions.

a1401.speaker: Julien Matter, Head of Mission of MSF in Guinea (on independence and funding)
a1401.name: Julien Matter
a1401.title: Head of Mission of MSF in Guinea (on independence and funding)
a1401.speech: Recalled that MSF's interventions, based on "impartiality, neutrality and independence", put the patient at the centre of concerns and benefit from effective logistics allowing rapid intervention in the event of disaster or epidemic; MSF works today in 70 countries, financed 98 per cent by private funds, thus guaranteeing its independence.

a1510.speaker: Donald Trump, Republican presidential candidate / former US President
a1510.name: Donald Trump
a1510.title: Republican presidential candidate / former US President
a1510.speech: Declared at a Republican rally in Pennsylvania: "Volodymyr Zelensky is the greatest salesman the world has ever known, because every time Volodymyr Zelensky goes to the United States, he leaves with about 60 billion dollars", adding: "He supports the Democratic Party and wants to see Vice President Kamala Harris become the next president of the United States."

a1510.speaker: Donald Trump, Republican presidential candidate / former US President
a1510.name: Donald Trump
a1510.title: Republican presidential candidate / former US President
a1510.speech: "If I win this election, the first thing I will do is call Zelensky and President Putin and tell them they have to make a deal" ; He did not specify what the terms of that deal might be.

a1510.speaker: Donald Trump, Republican presidential candidate / former US President
a1510.name: Donald Trump
a1510.title: Republican presidential candidate / former US President
a1510.speech: In the final days before the US elections he suddenly began saying that he was not friendly with Russia at all; he recently stated that he had "killed" and "stopped" the Nord Stream pipeline.

a1510.speaker: Russia
a1510.name: Russia
a1510.speech: Demands that the "new territorial realities" be recognised, that arms deliveries to Kyiv cease, and that the country's neutral status be consolidated.

a1510.speaker: Volodymyr Zelensky, President of Ukraine
a1510.name: Volodymyr Zelensky
a1510.title: President of Ukraine
a1510.speech: Admitted that if Donald Trump comes to power in the United States, there is a risk that arms deliveries to Kyiv will be reduced.

a1510.speaker: Politico
a1510.name: Politico
a1510.speech: Stressed: "Trump is sending a strong signal, but he will not support Ukraine and Zelensky against Putin."

a1510.speaker: Kamala Harris, Democratic Party presidential candidate / US Vice President
a1510.name: Kamala Harris
a1510.title: Democratic Party presidential candidate / US Vice President
a1510.speech: During a meeting with Volodymyr Zelensky she stressed that support for Kyiv was a strategic interest of the United States and not charity: "We support Ukraine not out of charity, but because the Ukrainian people and their future are in our strategic interest. It is in our interest to uphold international rules and norms."

a1510.speaker: Kamala Harris, Democratic Party presidential candidate / US Vice President
a1510.name: Kamala Harris
a1510.title: Democratic Party presidential candidate / US Vice President
a1510.speech: Said that if Donald Trump were president, then "Putin would be in Kyiv right now" ; "Let's be clear. He says he can end it on day one. Do you know what that means? We are talking about capitulation."

a1510.speaker: Kamala Harris, Democratic Party presidential candidate / US Vice President
a1510.name: Kamala Harris
a1510.title: Democratic Party presidential candidate / US Vice President
a1510.speech: Was keen to make it known that she would not continue Joe Biden's political course: "Like any new president who takes office, I will bring my life experiences, my professional experiences and fresh, new ideas" ; she could not promise Kyiv's accession to NATO, noting only that she would address the question "when and if the time comes."

a1510.speaker: Donald Trump and J.D. Vance, Republican presidential and vice-presidential candidates
a1510.name: Donald Trump and J.D. Vance
a1510.title: Republican presidential and vice-presidential candidates
a1510.speech: Have said they want to end the Russo-Ukrainian war quickly, which implies freezing the situation along the front line.

a1510.speaker: BFMTV
a1510.name: BFMTV
a1510.speech: Reporting Kamala Harris's position, where "she appears to want to align herself with the continuity of Joe Biden", warns that big questions arise in Kyiv about what this could mean, because Joe Biden's strategy can hardly be described as effective.

a1510.speaker: Volodymyr Zelensky, President of Ukraine
a1510.name: Volodymyr Zelensky
a1510.title: President of Ukraine
a1510.speech: Recently indicated that the country had received only 10% of the 60 billion dollars approved in April.

a1599.speaker: Government of Congo (DRC)
a1599.name: Government of Congo (DRC)
a1599.speech: Congo said the issue of liability has now been resolved.

a1599.speaker: Global health experts
a1599.name: Global health experts
a1599.speech: said the delay again showed the need for a better system to stop seemingly technical points holding up life-saving responses; global health experts and industry representatives said there should be a better system set up in advance of major outbreaks to cover the liability issue.

a1599.speaker: Samuel Roger Kamba Mulamba, Congo's health minister
a1599.name: Samuel Roger Kamba Mulamba
a1599.title: Congo's health minister
a1599.speech: "When I read the (donation) contract, I added that both countries must be responsible if any side-effects occur," said in a press conference in Kinshasa earlier this month. "That's why it took so long, because it went back to Japan." Now, "all the formalities have been completed," he added.

a1599.speaker: Japan's government
a1599.name: Japan's government
a1599.speech: told Reuters earlier this month there was no current dispute about liability, without going into further detail, and that discussions over deliveries were ongoing ; said on Tuesday it was "tackling and coordinating to solve these problems", without giving further detail.

a1599.speaker: KM Biologics, the Japanese company which produced the vaccine
a1599.name: KM Biologics
a1599.title: the Japanese company which produced the vaccine

a1599.speaker: Paula Barbosa, associate director of vaccine policy at the International Federation of Pharmaceutical Manufacturers and Associations (IFPMA)
a1599.name: Paula Barbosa
a1599.title: associate director of vaccine policy at the International Federation of Pharmaceutical Manufacturers and Associations (IFPMA)
a1599.speech: "During a pandemic, well-designed, no-fault compensation systems are essential."

a1599.speaker: One doctor working on the mpox response in Congo (anonymous)
a1599.name: One doctor working on the mpox response in Congo (anonymous)
a1599.speech: "It's important for these vaccines to arrive quickly." But, the doctor added, before widespread use, there should be tests on how to administer the vaccine, and a plan for where it would be most effective.

a1599.speaker: African health officials
a1599.name: African health officials
a1599.speech: say the roughly 375,000 doses of the Bavarian Nordic shot that have arrived in the country are still far short of what is needed.

a1599.speaker: Tatsuki Sato, Japan's Ministry of Health
a1599.name: Tatsuki Sato
a1599.title: Japan's Ministry of Health
a1599.speech: "We cannot tell you how to solve them immediately."

a1601.speaker: Augushito Davite, 69, and Patricia Lemeti, 42, Mozambican asylum seekers at Nyamithuthu Refugee Camp (speaking on behalf of other asylum seekers)
a1601.name: Augushito Davite
a1601.title: 69, and Patricia Lemeti, 42, Mozambican asylum seekers at Nyamithuthu Refugee Camp (speaking on behalf of other asylum seekers)
a1601.speech: Said the lack of food assistance is their most urgent need. "We are starving, the support being rendered is mostly non-food items," they shared.

a1601.speaker: Hilda Katema, Senior Administrative and Operations Manager, Malawi Department for Refugees
a1601.name: Hilda Katema
a1601.title: Senior Administrative and Operations Manager, Malawi Department for Refugees
a1601.speech: Acknowledged the crisis and assured that the government is committed to addressing the food needs of the asylum seekers.

a1601.speaker: Charles Kalemba, Commissioner, Malawi Department of Disaster Management Affairs (DoDMA)
a1601.name: Charles Kalemba
a1601.title: Commissioner, Malawi Department of Disaster Management Affairs (DoDMA)
a1601.speech: Confirmed that his department, in collaboration with the Department for Refugees, is working to ensure that the asylum seekers at Nyamithuthu camp receive essential supplies, including food ; emphasized the department's role in managing large numbers of people in camps and providing necessary expertise.

a1601.speaker: Gloria Nyang'iye, Associate Reporting Officer, UNHCR
a1601.name: Gloria Nyang'iye
a1601.title: Associate Reporting Officer, UNHCR
a1601.speech: Highlighted the progress in improving the camp's shelter and sanitation facilities, ensuring a more stable environment for the asylum seekers.

a1742.speaker: Miguel Thomas, WFP focal point for the project
a1742.name: Miguel Thomas
a1742.title: WFP focal point for the project
a1742.speech: Gave a welcome address opening the ceremony.

a1742.speaker: Mutinta Chimuka (WFP Representative and Country Director in Djibouti), Larry E. Andre (United States Ambassador to Djibouti) and Mohamed Abdallah (Secretary General of MENFOP)
a1742.name: Mutinta Chimuka (WFP Representative and Country Director in Djibouti)
a1742.title: Larry E. Andre (United States Ambassador to Djibouti) and Mohamed Abdallah (Secretary General of MENFOP)
a1742.speech: All recalled in their remarks that this work-study training forms part of the vocational training and capacity-building project in the transport and logistics sector implemented jointly by the Ministry of National Education and Vocational Training (MENFOP) and the World Food Programme (WFP), with the financial support of the United States Agency for International Development (USAID) in Djibouti.

a1773.speaker: Johannes Jozef Bults, Dutch entrepreneur engaged in import and export in the Qianhai and Shekou Area of Shenzhen
a1773.name: Johannes Jozef Bults
a1773.title: Dutch entrepreneur engaged in import and export in the Qianhai and Shekou Area of Shenzhen
a1773.speech: Noted that since the establishment of the zone, he has witnessed a continuous optimization of the business environment. "The government's support, from company registration to everyday operations, has made it incredibly convenient for entrepreneurs to do business here," he remarked.

a1773.speaker: Gu Qingyang, associate professor at the Lee Kuan Yew School of Public Policy, National University of Singapore
a1773.name: Gu Qingyang
a1773.title: associate professor at the Lee Kuan Yew School of Public Policy, National University of Singapore
a1773.speech: Expressed that China is currently at a critical stage of development. He anticipates that Guangdong will continue to embody the pioneering spirit of innovation and exploration, boldly venturing into avenues for high-quality development in China.

a1791.speaker: Dennis W. Hearne, U.S. Ambassador to Mozambique
a1791.name: Dennis W. Hearne
a1791.title: U.S. Ambassador to Mozambique
a1791.speech: "The humanitarian situation in northern Mozambique is concerning" ; "The U.S. Government remains committed to supporting the government of Mozambique and the Mozambican people to respond to this complex crisis" ; "This includes assisting the many Mozambican families and communities that have been hosting their neighbors, displaced from their homes due to violence in Cabo Delgado."

a1791.speaker: David Beasley, WFP Executive Director
a1791.name: David Beasley
a1791.title: WFP Executive Director
a1791.speech: "We are incredibly grateful for this generous contribution and the support of the United States here in Mozambique. Through WFP's life-saving assistance for families affected by conflict, we are planting the seeds of peace. But this is not enough" ; "We must work harder together to ensure the longer-term recovery and well-being of the people, helping them to move forward and giving them hope for a better future."

a1791.speaker: United States Agency for International Development (USAID) (official statement)
a1791.name: United States Agency for International Development (USAID) (official statement)
a1791.speech: Announced that the U.S. government, through USAID, awarded $30 million to the World Food Programme (WFP) to address food insecurity in communities affected by ongoing violence in Cabo Delgado and those affected by natural disasters in Sofala and Manica provinces, noting that the United States government is the largest donor to WFP in Mozambique, with a total of $130 million in contributions since 2018, and that the U.S. Government provides more than $500 million in annual assistance in Mozambique to improve the quality of healthcare and education, promote economic prosperity, and support the overall development of the nation.

a1879.speaker: Omar Abdi Saïd, Minister of Labour, in charge of Formalisation and Social Protection of Djibouti
a1879.name: Omar Abdi Saïd
a1879.title: Minister of Labour, in charge of Formalisation and Social Protection of Djibouti
a1879.speech: welcomed the new USAID representative, Ms Nancy Ostrowski, and expressed his best wishes for the accomplishment of her mission in Djibouti, a country of welcome and exchange; at the end of the meeting he expressed his thanks to the American people and to the officials of USAID, who spare no effort to support the government's actions in the fight against youth unemployment.

a1879.speaker: Nancy Ostrowski, new USAID representative in Djibouti
a1879.name: Nancy Ostrowski
a1879.title: new USAID representative in Djibouti
a1879.speech: welcomed the lasting and fruitful partnership with the Ministry of Labour and promised to continue and strengthen it within the framework of the Employment Initiatives project.

a1879.speaker: Both parties (Ministry of Labour and USAID)
a1879.name: Both parties (Ministry of Labour and USAID)
a1879.speech: committed at the end of the meeting to continuing their cooperative relations in the future.

a1950.speaker: Felix Kwakye Ofosu, Minister of Government Communications
a1950.name: Felix Kwakye Ofosu
a1950.title: Minister of Government Communications
a1950.speech: Announced in June this year that the government planned to construct approximately 600 CHPS compounds across the country by the end of 2025 as part of efforts to expand access to primary health care; according to the minister, the initiative will see each district constructing two new CHPS compounds this year, and he was optimistic that if the momentum was sustained, the country could exceed 2,000 CHPS compounds over the next four years.

a1950.speaker: Studies (on CHPS)
a1950.name: Studies (on CHPS)
a1950.speech: Studies have shown that CHPS has contributed to a decline in under-five mortality rates, especially among the poorest and least educated populations.

a1950.speaker: Authors of the study “Implementation of the community-based health planning services (CHPS) in rural and urban Ghana: a history and systematic review of what works, for whom and why”
a1950.name: Authors of the study “Implementation of the community-based health planning services (CHPS) in rural and urban Ghana: a history and systematic review of what works
a1950.title: for whom and why”
a1950.speech: Conclude that a review of service provision to prepare and respond to pandemics, prevalence of non-communicable diseases and adaptation to changing community contexts, particularly urbanisation, are required for the successful delivery and future scale-up of CHPS.

a1992.speaker: Government of Cabo Verde
a1992.name: Government of Cabo Verde
a1992.speech: Announced the continuation of privatisations with the selection of a strategic partner for CV Handling and the sale of 10% of the shares to emigrants and to the company’s workers; launched the “Cabo Verde Brand” in tourism and the “Renewable Energy Storage Plant” on the island of Santiago in energy.

a1992.speaker: Prime Minister of Cabo Verde
a1992.name: Prime Minister of Cabo Verde
a1992.speech: said that with the new “Cabo Verde Brand” the aim is to “transform each island into a tourist destination that is authentic, genuine and differentiating.”

a1992.speaker: World Bank
a1992.name: World Bank
a1992.speech: notes that the knock-on effect of tourism on the economy is already 40%.

a2003.speaker: Abdirashid Fidow, Deputy Chief Executive of the Anti-Tribalism Movement, political analyst and social justice campaigner (opinion piece)
a2003.name: Abdirashid Fidow
a2003.title: Deputy Chief Executive of the Anti-Tribalism Movement, political analyst and social justice campaigner (opinion piece)
a2003.speech: writes that more than a decade after Somalia adopted federalism as a post-conflict solution, the system remains at odds with the realities on the ground, and that unless urgently reformed or replaced, Somalia’s federal experiment may deepen the very fragmentation it sought to prevent; argues that Somalia’s federalism is largely clan-based and has reinforced exclusionary politics, that without a finalised federal constitution federalism remains based on conflicting interpretations, that Al-Shabaab has stepped into the cracks of fragmented authority, and that federalism has become a stage for foreign ambitions: “Unless federalism is reimagined through a Somali-led, inclusive, and sovereign framework, the very idea of a unified Somalia risks fading into history.”

a2117.speaker: John Lual Akol Akol, chairperson of the East African Business Council (EABC)
a2117.name: John Lual Akol Akol
a2117.title: chairperson of the East African Business Council (EABC)
a2117.speech: Called for a unified African stance and stronger collaboration between the public and private sectors to leverage the policy shifts: "Africa must position itself as a key player in global trade, particularly as the U.S. administration redefines its approach to international business relations."

a2117.speaker: John Thomas, Nestpoint Associates
a2117.name: John Thomas
a2117.title: Nestpoint Associates
a2117.speech: Outlined the transactional nature of the new U.S. administration's trade policies: "Africa has a unique opportunity to benefit from increased U.S. tariffs on China by positioning itself as an alternative supply chain hub" ; also highlighted Africa's growing potential in the technology sector, particularly in data centers, which could serve as a valuable asset for future economic expansion.

a2117.speaker: Jas Bedi, chairperson of the Kenya Private Sector Alliance (KEPSA) and vice chairperson of EABC
a2117.name: Jas Bedi
a2117.title: chairperson of the Kenya Private Sector Alliance (KEPSA) and vice chairperson of EABC
a2117.speech: Discussed the global trade shift from globalization to regionalization and localization of global brands, and pointed to the expiration of the African Growth and Opportunity Act (AGOA) on September 30, 2025: "AGOA has been instrumental in bolstering U.S.-Africa trade relations, but as its expiration nears, we must prepare for the future."

a2117.speaker: Jas Bedi, chairperson of the Kenya Private Sector Alliance (KEPSA) and vice chairperson of EABC
a2117.name: Jas Bedi
a2117.title: chairperson of the Kenya Private Sector Alliance (KEPSA) and vice chairperson of EABC
a2117.speech: Noted that Africa's economy accounts for only 3.5% of the global economy and contributes just 2% of U.S. imports, suggesting the continent does not pose major competition in terms of global market share or geopolitical influence, and emphasized Africa's demographic advantage: "We must capitalize on this asset by focusing on value-added commodities and fostering regional integration."

a2117.speaker: Michael P. Murphy, chief strategy officer at Fairfield Management and senior advisor to Africa at Nestpoint Associates
a2117.name: Michael P. Murphy
a2117.title: chief strategy officer at Fairfield Management and senior advisor to Africa at Nestpoint Associates
a2117.speech: Described the ongoing U.S. policy shifts as a historic opportunity to redefine trade and investment relations with Africa: "This is a historic opportunity for the U.S. to unlock capital and invest more deeply in Africa. The new U.S. administration is eager to prioritize greater American investment in Africa."

a2117.speaker: Dr. Valencia de la Vega, expert in manufacturing leadership and supply chain management
a2117.name: Dr. Valencia de la Vega
a2117.title: expert in manufacturing leadership and supply chain management
a2117.speech: Spoke about the importance of optimizing transportation between Africa and the U.S. through AI-driven logistics solutions: "AI-driven logistics can dramatically improve transportation between Africa and the U.S., unlocking new efficiencies for trade" ; also highlighted key trade and investment sectors, including renewable energy, battery production, textiles, and the research and development of value-added manufacturing.

a2117.speaker: Simon Kaheru, EABC Vice Chairperson
a2117.name: Simon Kaheru
a2117.title: EABC Vice Chairperson
a2117.speech: "Africa must move beyond its reliance on aid and focus on trade as the pathway to long-term development."

a2117.speaker: Adrian Njau, acting executive director of EABC
a2117.name: Adrian Njau
a2117.title: acting executive director of EABC
a2117.speech: "We are here to discuss how current policy shifts can turn into actionable opportunities for Africa's economic transformation."

a2117.speaker: U.S. International Trade Commission
a2117.name: U.S. International Trade Commission
a2117.speech: According to the Commission, African countries benefiting from AGOA exported approximately $103 billion worth of non-crude products to the U.S. between 2001 and 2022.

a2206.speaker: Hawa Loleyah Norris, Superintendent of Bong County
a2206.name: Hawa Loleyah Norris
a2206.title: Superintendent of Bong County
a2206.speech: Emphasized the importance of community consensus in such decisions: "All that we agree on here today, I want to ensure it is the decision of all the people in all the affected communities through their representatives here present." ; assured the citizens that their concerns and recommendations would be forwarded to the Bong County Legislative Caucus and the national government for consideration ; led an in-depth discussion on each point raised to ensure the document accurately reflected the views and aspirations of all citizen groups.

a2206.speaker: Hawa Loleyah Norris, Superintendent of Bong County
a2206.name: Hawa Loleyah Norris
a2206.title: Superintendent of Bong County
a2206.speech: Acknowledged the importance of making demands for community development but stressed that communities affected by ArcelorMittal Liberia's operations must recognize the value of the concession's presence and work to protect its investments: "While it is good to make demands, communities impacted by ArcelorMittal Liberia's operations need to embrace the operation of the concession and protect its investments." ; highlighted the mounting economic challenges faced by the government and pointed out that concession agreements such as ArcelorMittal's are crucial in supporting social development initiatives, particularly in light of the USAID drawdown, which has impacted funding for various programs.

a2206.speaker: Hawa Loleyah Norris, Superintendent of Bong County
a2206.name: Hawa Loleyah Norris
a2206.title: Superintendent of Bong County
a2206.speech: Cautioned: "Development cannot come if we continue to fight among ourselves and tear each other down. We need to come together, to move the county and district forward so that we change the way our communities look."

a2206.speaker: Petition from the rail-impacted communities of Bong County
a2206.name: Petition from the rail-impacted communities of Bong County
a2206.speech: Acknowledged AML's contributions to Liberia's economic growth, job creation, infrastructure development, education, and healthcare, but highlighted challenges including insufficient employment for local residents, environmental hazards, damage to roads and infrastructure, and delays in compensation for property damage; proposed an increase in social development funds to match AML's expanded production, prioritization of local employment and skills training, a legally binding rail corridor development fund, improved environmental protection measures, expanded social infrastructure commitments, repairs to roads and bridges, adequate compensation for affected residents, and enhanced safety measures along the rail corridor. "We appreciate your leadership and look forward to your support in ensuring that this agreement delivers tangible benefits to our communities," the petition stated.

a2206.speaker: Community members of the rail-impacted communities
a2206.name: Community members of the rail-impacted communities
a2206.speech: Expressed optimism that their voices would be heard and that their proposed measures would lead to meaningful improvements in their livelihoods and local development.

a2693.speaker: Doyo Hassan Doyo, National League for Democracy (NLD) presidential candidate
a2693.name: Doyo Hassan Doyo
a2693.title: National League for Democracy (NLD) presidential candidate
a2693.speech: Has promised sweeping reforms in healthcare, economic empowerment and social equality if elected in the October General Election. Addressing party supporters at Mabawa Commercial, Pangani Bus Stand in Tanga Region on Thursday, the opposition leader presented the NLD manifesto, built around six guiding pillars: patriotism, justice, inclusive development, equality, accountability and governance grounded in national ethics.

a2693.speaker: Doyo Hassan Doyo, NLD presidential candidate (on maternal health)
a2693.name: Doyo Hassan Doyo
a2693.title: NLD presidential candidate (on maternal health)
a2693.speech: Emphasised that one of the party’s immediate priorities would be free maternal health services. He criticised the fact that Tanzanian women still pay for delivery decades after independence, calling it “unacceptable and unconscionable.” “It is inconceivable that a nation which gained her independence 64 years ago still charges mothers 100,000/- to give birth. How do you tax a person who is yet to be born? NLD will end this burden. You have a choice—free delivery services under NLD or continue paying for the service under the ruling party,” he declared.

a2693.speaker: Doyo Hassan Doyo, NLD presidential candidate (on leaders’ pay and conduct)
a2693.name: Doyo Hassan Doyo
a2693.title: NLD presidential candidate (on leaders’ pay and conduct)
a2693.speech: Condemned what he termed “unpatriotic behaviour” by leaders who treat parliamentary seats as business ventures. Pledged to reduce MPs’ salaries to 1.5m/- per month while significantly raising the pay of professionals such as doctors to 12m/-. “Our leadership will serve the people, not private interests,” he said.

a2693.speaker: Doyo Hassan Doyo, NLD presidential candidate (on economic policy)
a2693.name: Doyo Hassan Doyo
a2693.title: NLD presidential candidate (on economic policy)
a2693.speech: Promised to empower households and create sustainable livelihoods, moving citizens beyond petty trade into profitable enterprises. Said his administration would promote local value addition to natural resources, including minerals, to generate revenue, reduce poverty and clear national debts within five years using domestic revenues. Pledged to invest in Tanzania’s blue economy, including purchasing a deepsea fishing vessel to expand the fishing industry, with fish processed locally for both domestic consumption and export, creating jobs for youths and increasing foreign exchange earnings.

a2693.speaker: Doyo Hassan Doyo, NLD presidential candidate (on education)
a2693.name: Doyo Hassan Doyo
a2693.title: NLD presidential candidate (on education)
a2693.speech: Promised free, practical education at all levels to equip citizens with skills for employment and entrepreneurship. He said graduates must be competitive in the job market or capable of creating their own employment, emphasising the need to harness Tanzania’s natural resources to attract investment and generate local wealth without reliance on foreign loans.

a2693.speaker: Doyo Hassan Doyo, NLD presidential candidate (on justice and security laws)
a2693.name: Doyo Hassan Doyo
a2693.title: NLD presidential candidate (on justice and security laws)
a2693.speech: Highlighted social justice as a core objective, pledging to establish effective legal systems that deliver justice without citizens having to “chase” it. He also vowed to repeal the Anti-Terrorism Act within 90 days, arguing that it has been misused to discriminate and that Tanzania currently faces no real terrorist threat.

a2693.speaker: Doyo Hassan Doyo, NLD presidential candidate (on rural development and inclusive leadership)
a2693.name: Doyo Hassan Doyo
a2693.title: NLD presidential candidate (on rural development and inclusive leadership)
a2693.speech: Outlined plans to develop rural industries, use local resources efficiently and strengthen public services. He stressed that leadership should be inclusive, prioritising citizens’ welfare regardless of gender, religion, ethnicity or economic status.

a2693.speaker: Doyo Hassan Doyo, NLD presidential candidate (on campaign conduct)
a2693.name: Doyo Hassan Doyo
a2693.title: NLD presidential candidate (on campaign conduct)
a2693.speech: Accused ruling party mobilisation units of disrupting proceedings with vehicles blaring campaign songs nearby, pledging to report the incident to the Ethics Committee and urging peaceful and fair campaigning across the country.

a2693.speaker: Doyo Hassan Doyo, NLD presidential candidate (closing remarks)
a2693.name: Doyo Hassan Doyo
a2693.title: NLD presidential candidate (closing remarks)
a2693.speech: “Our vision is to build a new Tanzania—one grounded in inclusive development, social justice and a resilient domestic economy. We have a clear strategy and a structured plan for transformative leadership,” Doyo said, concluding to cheers from supporters.

a2722.speaker: Public data on United States foreign assistance (USAID official figures)
a2722.name: Public data on United States foreign assistance (USAID official figures)
a2722.speech: show that USAID disbursed a total of 72 billion dollars in fiscal year 2023, with more than 16.6 billion dollars sent to Ukraine; within the CPLP, Mozambique received 664.122 million dollars, Angola 71.320 million, Brazil 68.985 million, Timor-Leste 43.688 million, Cabo Verde 2.961 million, Guinea-Bissau 2.910 million, Equatorial Guinea 658,700 dollars, Sao Tome and Principe 216,379 dollars and Portugal 6,482 dollars.

a2722.speaker: Marco Rubio, US Secretary of State and new acting director of USAID
a2722.name: Marco Rubio
a2722.title: US Secretary of State and new acting director of USAID
a2722.speech: accused USAID of being "completely devoid of responsiveness", criticising the "insubordination" in that body.

a2722.speaker: Donald Trump, Elon Musk (head of the Department of Government Efficiency) and some Republican members of Congress
a2722.name: Donald Trump
a2722.title: Elon Musk (head of the Department of Government Efficiency) and some Republican members of Congress
a2722.speech: have criticised USAID - which oversees humanitarian, development and security programmes in about 120 countries - in increasingly harsh terms, accusing it of promoting progressive causes.

a2722.speaker: Experts (unnamed)
a2722.name: Experts (unnamed)
a2722.speech: assessed that the effects on HIV programmes are not yet clear, but the consequences could be rapid and even dangerous.

a2722.speaker: Maria Benvinda Levi, Mozambican Prime Minister
a2722.name: Maria Benvinda Levi
a2722.title: Mozambican Prime Minister
a2722.speech: admitted last week that the health sector will be the most affected by this suspension of funding for aid programmes by the American administration. "It is a big challenge because the support of the United States is extremely important support, particularly in the social areas. So, we will have to see, with our own resources, how we can redirect some resources to those areas, so that they are not left without any structure for carrying out their activities." ; "The main [American] support is for the health area, but there are other sectors that receive less significant support."

a2760.speaker: UNICEF (press release / new data)
a2760.name: UNICEF (press release / new data)
a2760.speech: Sounds the alarm and expresses a need for an additional $200 million this year to maintain and expand essential nutrition services, particularly in Darfur where acute child malnutrition remains rampant; according to new data published by UNICEF, the nutritional situation of children in Sudan is reaching catastrophic levels, with a 46% rise in the number of children treated for severe acute malnutrition in the Darfur region between January and May 2025, and more than 40,000 children admitted in North Darfur for treatment for severe acute malnutrition in the first five months of the year, double the number recorded in the same period last year; admissions for severe acute malnutrition jumped by more than 70% in North Kordofan, 174% in Khartoum State and 683% in Al Jazirah State; UNICEF calls on all parties to facilitate rapid, safe and unhindered access for humanitarian aid to affected populations and has appealed to donor countries for an additional $200 million this year.

a2760.speaker: Sheldon Yett, UNICEF Representative in Sudan
a2760.name: Sheldon Yett
a2760.title: UNICEF Representative in Sudan
a2760.speech: "The children of Darfur are starving because of the conflict and deprived of the aid that could save their lives." ; "We are at a critical moment: children's lives depend on whether the world decides to act or to look away."

a2760.speaker: Latest surveys conducted in the five regions of Darfur (April-May 2025)
a2760.name: Latest surveys conducted in the five regions of Darfur (April-May 2025)
a2760.speech: Reveal an alarming situation: in 9 of the 13 localities the acute malnutrition rate has exceeded the emergency levels set by the World Health Organization; particularly worrying is the locality of Yasin, in East Darfur, where the May survey reveals a global acute malnutrition rate of 28% - if that figure reaches 30% it will cross one of the three critical thresholds set for declaring a famine.

a3022.speaker: Songa Lawrence, Chair of the Parliamentary Forum on Climate Change (PFCC) in the Ugandan Parliament
a3022.name: Songa Lawrence
a3022.title: Chair of the Parliamentary Forum on Climate Change (PFCC) in the Ugandan Parliament
a3022.speech: In his opening address, encouraged climatologists to identify gaps and called on decision-makers to play their part in filling those gaps; stressed that decision-makers should be convinced of the crucial role of climate forecasting and of disseminating information to end users.

a3022.speaker: Guleid Artan, Director of the IGAD Climate Prediction and Applications Centre (ICPAC)
a3022.name: Guleid Artan
a3022.title: Director of the IGAD Climate Prediction and Applications Centre (ICPAC)
a3022.speech: Stated that by “bringing together countries with shared climatological characteristics, the forum guaranteed consistency in access to climate information and in its interpretation.”

a3022.speaker: GHACOF 51 regional consensus climate outlook (March-May 2019)
a3022.name: GHACOF 51 regional consensus climate outlook (March-May 2019)
a3022.speech: Points to an increased probability of near-normal rainfall over much of the GHA region, increased probability of wetness over central and north-western Tanzania, Burundi, Rwanda, much of Uganda, western and northern Kenya and southern and south-eastern Ethiopia, suppressed rainfall in the far south of Tanzania and central coastal Somalia, above-normal average temperatures over much of the GHA, an earlier-than-normal onset of the rains over most of the equatorial region, and a likely earlier-than-normal cessation of rainfall in south-eastern Ethiopia, central and southern Somalia, eastern Kenya, south-eastern Uganda and northern Tanzania.

a3077.speaker: Alassane Ouédraogo, Secretary General of Burkina Faso’s Ministry of Industry, Commerce and Crafts
a3077.name: Alassane Ouédraogo
a3077.title: Secretary General of Burkina Faso’s Ministry of Industry, Commerce and Crafts
a3077.speech: Said the meeting is a continuation of the commitments made by the AES Heads of State when they signed the Treaty establishing the Confederation of Sahel States on 6 July 2024 in Niamey, with the clearly stated aim of creating a unifying framework to encourage the region’s economic integration through concrete measures and strong commitments; he indicated that the meeting aims to allow the experts to make progress on defining the practical arrangements for implementing the recommendations of the first ministerial meeting held on 19 October 2024 in Bamako, which was a decisive step in building a genuine economic and commercial community within the AES.

a3077.speaker: Alassane Ouédraogo, Secretary General of Burkina Faso’s Ministry of Industry, Commerce and Crafts
a3077.name: Alassane Ouédraogo
a3077.title: Secretary General of Burkina Faso’s Ministry of Industry, Commerce and Crafts
a3077.speech: “The recommendations from your work in Bamako are of paramount importance for the economic development of our area. They aim not only to harmonise the institutional business framework, but also and above all to facilitate trade and strengthen regional cooperation between private sector actors.”

a3077.speaker: Alassane Ouédraogo, Secretary General of Burkina Faso’s Ministry of Industry, Commerce and Crafts
a3077.name: Alassane Ouédraogo
a3077.title: Secretary General of Burkina Faso’s Ministry of Industry, Commerce and Crafts
a3077.speech: Noted that the experts will concretely examine the priority actions that will strengthen regional integration, the challenges to be overcome to improve the free movement of goods and people, and the financing mechanisms to support strategic economic sectors that will facilitate the transition towards a genuine free trade area ; “The experts are therefore expected to propose concrete solutions to the recommendations made, with clear timetables and adequate resources. It is this work of reflection and consensus that will make it possible to advance the project of the Confederation of Sahel States and to build a prosperous economic future for our countries.”

a3077.speaker: Ali Samba Diabiri, Secretary General of Niger’s Ministry of Commerce and Industry and head of the Nigerien experts’ delegation
a3077.name: Ali Samba Diabiri
a3077.title: Secretary General of Niger’s Ministry of Commerce and Industry and head of the Nigerien experts’ delegation
a3077.speech: Welcomed the holding of this experts’ meeting, which will make it possible to take stock not only of the implementation of the recommendations made by the ministers at their first meeting, but also of the memoranda of understanding signed between the chambers of commerce and the chambers of agriculture of the three countries; for him, this framework for exchange will make it possible to draw up an action plan through priority actions to be defined ; “Together, with the private sector, we will work on the implementation of this action plan so that we can contribute significantly to achieving the objectives assigned to the pillars of AES development.”

a3105.speaker: Somalia Multi-Stakeholder Climate Outlook Forum (climate outlook released September 3, 2025)
a3105.name: Somalia Multi-Stakeholder Climate Outlook Forum (climate outlook released September 3
a3105.speech: Warns that the majority of the country will likely face drier-than-normal conditions and above-average temperatures. The Deyr 2025 seasonal outlook indicates most of Somalia will receive below-average rainfall, with the highest probability (55%) for drier-than-average conditions in Jubaland, Southwest State, Hirshabelle and Galmudug, while some localized areas within Puntland and the Northeast are expected to experience near-normal rainfall. The forecast predicts warmer-than-average temperatures across the entire country, a normal onset of rains in North and Central Somalia (September 24 to October 4) and a delayed start in the southern regions (October 14 to November 3). It suggests current humanitarian needs may worsen, leading to increased food and water insecurity, displacement, and a heightened risk of conflict over scarce resources.

a3105.speaker: Somalia Multi-Stakeholder Climate Outlook Forum
a3105.name: Somalia Multi-Stakeholder Climate Outlook Forum
a3105.speech: Issued a call for preparedness, urging a coordinated response from all stakeholders: government and humanitarian agencies are advised to scale up early warning systems and drought response efforts; farmers and livestock keepers are encouraged to adopt drought-resilient practices such as water conservation and planting drought-resistant crops; health and disaster management authorities have been put on alert to prepare for potential outbreaks of heat-related illnesses and vector-borne diseases like malaria and dengue; and development partners and NGOs are requested to provide timely humanitarian assistance, focusing particularly on the most vulnerable and affected regions.

a3142.speaker: Linda Thomas-Greenfield, United States Special Envoy/Ambassador to the United Nations
a3142.name: Linda Thomas-Greenfield
a3142.title: United States Special Envoy/Ambassador to the United Nations
a3142.speech: has made one point clear in her speeches with African leaders that “African nations are free to buy grain from Russia but could face consequences if they trade in U.S.-sanctioned commodities such as oil from Russia” ; “Countries can buy Russian agricultural products, including fertilizer and wheat” ; “if a country decides to engage with Russia, where there are sanctions, then they are breaking those sanctions. We caution countries not to break those sanctions because then ... they stand the chance of having actions taken against them.”

a3142.speaker: Alexander Surikov, Russian Ambassador to Mozambique
a3142.name: Alexander Surikov
a3142.title: Russian Ambassador to Mozambique
a3142.speech: after a meeting with the Confederation of Economic Associations of Mozambique (CTA), had proposed that the Mozambican authorities could buy Russian oil in roubles, after Moscow presented the option to Maputo; further expressed Russian companies’ continuing interest in investing in Mozambique; likewise, the possibility was raised of Russia opening a bank in Mozambique focused on supporting bilateral trade and investment; raised how Mozambican companies could have direct access to Russian wheat suppliers ; “The rouble and the metical are worthy currencies that do not need the benevolence of some other countries that control the international system,” the Russian diplomat explained, adding that Moscow wanted to strengthen cooperation with Maputo.

a3142.speaker: Carlos Zacarias, Minister of Mineral Resources and Energy of Mozambique
a3142.name: Carlos Zacarias
a3142.title: Minister of Mineral Resources and Energy of Mozambique
a3142.speech: admitted the possibility of buying Russian oil in roubles: “I am sure that we will study and verify the feasibility of this offer from Russia. If it is viable, for sure Russian oil will be acquired in roubles.”

a3142.speaker: Confederation of Economic Associations of Mozambique (CTA) data
a3142.name: Confederation of Economic Associations of Mozambique (CTA) data
a3142.speech: According to data provided by CTA, the annual volume of economic transactions between Mozambique and Russia is estimated to be, at least, US$100 million (€98.5 million at current exchange rates).

a3142.speaker: Ministry of Mineral Resources and Energy of Mozambique (data)
a3142.name: Ministry of Mineral Resources and Energy of Mozambique (data)
a3142.speech: Mozambique has proven reserves of over 180 trillion cubic feet, according to data from the Ministry of Mineral Resources and Energy.

a3337.speaker: Mary Gyamfia, plantain trader in the Ashaiman and Tema Community One markets
a3337.name: Mary Gyamfia
a3337.title: plantain trader in the Ashaiman and Tema Community One markets
a3337.speech: "I used to sell tomatoes, but I incurred so many losses due to the short life span and also poor handling during transportation." ; "The plantain business is far better than the tomatoes. When I started, I shared space with other traders to get a truck full, but I'm now able to buy a truck full of plantains alone to distribute to my customers."

a3337.speaker: Mary Gyamfia, plantain trader in the Ashaiman and Tema Community One markets
a3337.name: Mary Gyamfia
a3337.title: plantain trader in the Ashaiman and Tema Community One markets
a3337.speech: "Whether plantains are in season or not, the drivers charge according to fuel prices. Another issue is the high cost of oil. As a result, chips producers are unable to buy plantains in large quantities as they used to."

a3337.speaker: Augustina Avinu, trader who used to run a local 'chopbar' restaurant
a3337.name: Augustina Avinu
a3337.title: trader who used to run a local 'chopbar' restaurant
a3337.speech: Says the sellers who travel hundreds of kilometres to source plantains currently compete with other traders from neighbouring countries like Togo, Cote d'Ivoire and Burkina Faso, as the farmers claim they offer better pricing: "The government should consider regulating fuel prices, which would ease transportation costs for us and help plantain chips producers who are struggling with high oil prices. This is slowing the business growth."

a3337.speaker: Agness Bekoe, small-scale plantain chips producer
a3337.name: Agness Bekoe
a3337.title: small-scale plantain chips producer
a3337.speech: "Because of the airtight paper pouches I use to package it, people travelling abroad buy it a lot, and this was a result of recommendations from friends and customers. This is what has kept the business moving."

a3337.speaker: Agness Bekoe, small-scale plantain chips producer
a3337.name: Agness Bekoe
a3337.title: small-scale plantain chips producer
a3337.speech: Corroborated Gyamfia and Avinu's submission on how costly fresh plantains and oil have been lately, and believes post-harvest losses in the markets are still an issue because of the high cost of plantains: "Price increments are regular even in the peak season, so even if you're willing to buy more to process, the capital is not enough. It's disappointing to see heaps of overripe plantains when they could have been sold in their fresh state."

a3337.speaker: Charity Adupong, Food Processing Entrepreneur and Founder of Meannan Foods
a3337.name: Charity Adupong
a3337.title: Food Processing Entrepreneur and Founder of Meannan Foods
a3337.speech: Believes the food processing and preservation industry in Ghana has not reached its peak, and so the influx of noodles is infiltrating the system, such that "most children don't even want to eat our indigenous foods, and it's also due to the fact that the preparation of these foods takes longer to cook" ; "Ghana fufu is mostly made from plantain and cassava. We all love our fufu, but it takes a lot of time to make, and these are the reasons we need to process our foods to make it easy for people to eat while preserving traditional recipes, and so this is what inspired me to start processing plantain."

a3337.speaker: Charity Adupong, Food Processing Entrepreneur and Founder of Meannan Foods
a3337.name: Charity Adupong
a3337.title: Food Processing Entrepreneur and Founder of Meannan Foods
a3337.speech: "Sometimes you order plantain from the farmers or market queens, and in the process of transportation, things do not go your way. It is not as fresh as you want it, so we decided that instead of returning it to the farmer, we have to find something else to do with it, and that's how we also started our plantain chips production." ; "My love for roasted plantains and peanuts also influenced me to give the Meannan plantain chips a twist by adding coated fried peanuts, which makes them different from the regular ones on the market."

a3337.speaker: Charity Adupong, Food Processing Entrepreneur and Founder of Meannan Foods
a3337.name: Charity Adupong
a3337.title: Food Processing Entrepreneur and Founder of Meannan Foods
a3337.speech: "Part of the work I'm now doing with the Food Research Institute and some other organisations is to find ways of having plantains all year round, with which we will be able to process more." ; "With the kind of work we do, when plantain is in season, we do not have too much waste as was the case a few years ago. Plantain is seasonal, so if we do not take advantage of processing to extend the shelf life, then we're doomed."

a3337.speaker: Kwame Antwi Boasiako, plantain farmer and marketer in Asamankese, Eastern Region
a3337.name: Kwame Antwi Boasiako
a3337.title: plantain farmer and marketer in Asamankese, Eastern Region
a3337.speech: Believes there's a high demand for the starchy tropical fruit, however the farmers are at a disadvantage due to poor pricing from the market women: "Farmers need to understand marketing and plant accordingly. Planting monthly gives a better assurance of profit-making by harvesting all year round. The demand is there, and I have people I supply to in the cities."

a3337.speaker: Kojo Akoto Boateng, Agribusiness Strategist
a3337.name: Kojo Akoto Boateng
a3337.title: Agribusiness Strategist
