a3337.speech: Says these innovations need proper attention not only to address unemployment but also climate change by creating an industry out of the whole tree to replace single-use plastics and other products in the ecosystem: "If we had a well-organised plantain market, we could aggregate plantains as well as the peels for animal feed production, while the leaves can be used for food packaging instead of using plastics to wrap hot foods." ; "Once you harvest plantain and banana, the plant becomes waste apart from the suckers that grow around the mother. The stem also presents a big opportunity for us to do proper mulching instead of using plastic. It contains a lot of moisture and delivers more moisture to the plants and decomposes to add more nutrients to the soil."

a3374.speaker: Insiders (anonymous)
a3374.name: Insiders (anonymous)
a3374.speech: Say that then Minister of Energy Dipuo Peters played a big role in the long windy road to the Paris accord, making her one of the unsung heroes of reaching the global accord.

a3374.speaker: Glencore
a3374.name: Glencore
a3374.speech: Says that R150/tonne — the price Eskom refuses to exceed for coal delivered from the Glencore-operated Optimum mine — is less than what it costs to mine the coal.

a3374.speaker: International Energy Agency (IEA)
a3374.name: International Energy Agency (IEA)
a3374.speech: According to the IEA, in 2012 the cost of coal represented 27% of Eskom’s total operating costs, reflecting Eskom’s relatively low fuel costs.

a3374.speaker: Eskom
a3374.name: Eskom
a3374.speech: Says that its cost plus mines’ production rapidly deteriorated since 2007 and that, every year since, they have performed below their own budgets.

a3374.speaker: Eskom
a3374.name: Eskom
a3374.speech: Describes the coming coal shortages as a 40 Mtpa requirement, which translates into about 10 new mines that need to be opened up in South Africa for Eskom’s requirements alone ; estimated in 2013 that the capital expenditure to meet this requirement amounted to R100 billion alone.

a3374.speaker: Macquarie Bank (2013 study)
a3374.name: Macquarie Bank (2013 study)
a3374.speech: According to a study done by Macquarie Bank in 2013, transport and beneficiation costs push delivered costs of coal from the Waterberg to R410/ton, even though production costs for Waterberg coal are much cheaper.

a3374.speaker: Coal Atlas
a3374.name: Coal Atlas
a3374.speech: Cited as the source for the time scales in which coal developed and for the figures on coal reserves — deposits that can be exploited economically using current technology estimated at 968 gigatonnes, with vast additional deposits proven but currently uneconomic to exploit amounting to 22,000 gigatonnes.

a3407.speaker: United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA) research
a3407.name: United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA) research
a3407.speech: Research from UNFPA indicates that for every dollar invested in family planning, there is an estimated return of $8.78 in benefits to families and society, translating to a potential economic benefit of approximately N1.06 trillion ($660 billion) by 2050.

a3407.speaker: Dr. Samukeliso Dube, Executive Director of FP2030
a3407.name: Dr. Samukeliso Dube
a3407.title: Executive Director of FP2030
a3407.speech: Emphasizes that family planning is not merely a health service but a fundamental human right that must be prioritized, especially in light of recent global cuts in foreign aid.

a3548.speaker: Volodymyr Zelensky, President of Ukraine
a3548.name: Volodymyr Zelensky
a3548.title: President of Ukraine
a3548.speech: Said on Friday that he was ready to accept NATO protection guarantees limited at first to the territories controlled by Kyiv in order to “end the hot phase of the war” waged by Russia, suggesting he was willing to wait before recovering the areas occupied by the Russian army if such an agreement could provide security for the rest of Ukraine and end the fighting: “If we want to end the hot phase of the war, we must place under NATO’s umbrella the territory of Ukraine that we control,” he told Sky News. “That is what we must do quickly, and then Ukraine can recover the other part of its territory by diplomatic means.”

a3548.speaker: Volodymyr Zelensky, President of Ukraine
a3548.name: Volodymyr Zelensky
a3548.title: President of Ukraine
a3548.speech: Insisted that any offer of NATO membership had to be made to the whole of Ukraine, and stressed: “If we are talking about a ceasefire, we need guarantees that Putin will not come back.”

a3548.speaker: Vladimir Putin, President of Russia
a3548.name: Vladimir Putin
a3548.title: President of Russia
a3548.speech: Demands that the Ukrainian army withdraw from more territory and refuses any NATO membership for Ukraine, and has already asked Kyiv to give up its ambitions of joining NATO if it wants a peace agreement ; threatened to strike decision-making centres in the Ukrainian capital with his new “Oreshnik” missile in response to the firing of US- and UK-supplied missiles onto Russian territory.

a3548.speaker: Kyiv (Ukrainian government)
a3548.name: Kyiv (Ukrainian government)
a3548.speech: Has until now always ruled out ceding territory in exchange for peace.

a3548.speaker: Donald Trump, US President-elect
a3548.name: Donald Trump
a3548.title: US President-elect
a3548.speech: Has criticised American aid to Kyiv and claimed during his campaign that he could end the conflict within hours, without however saying how.

a3548.speaker: Emmanuel Macron, President of France (via the French presidency)
a3548.name: Emmanuel Macron
a3548.title: President of France (via the French presidency)
a3548.speech: “Condemned in the strongest terms Russia’s indiscriminate strikes, which keep intensifying against the cities, against civilians and against Ukraine’s energy infrastructure,” the French presidency said ; “These strikes, the increased cooperation with North Korea, and the irresponsible rhetoric that accompanies them, are part of an unacceptable logic of escalation on Russia’s part,” Mr Macron added.

a3548.speaker: Matthew Miller, US State Department spokesman
a3548.name: Matthew Miller
a3548.title: US State Department spokesman
a3548.speech: Said that US Secretary of State Antony Blinken spoke on Friday with Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha to brief him on “American objectives regarding enduring support for Ukraine.”

a3559.speaker: Winnie Byanyima, UNAIDS executive director
a3559.name: Winnie Byanyima
a3559.title: UNAIDS executive director
a3559.speech: Said the world risks returning to the worst days of the global AIDS pandemic following the sudden halt to US foreign aid funding, warning millions would die: if the US funding is not reinstated or others do not step in to fill the gap, “there will be an additional… 6.3 million AIDS-related deaths”, a 10-fold increase, in the next four years alone ; “You’re talking of losing the gains that we have made over the last 25 years. It is very serious,” she told reporters in Geneva ; “It is reasonable for the United States to want to reduce its funding over time, but the sudden withdrawal of life-saving support is having a devastating impact.” ; “The US cuts mean that today, 27 countries in Africa and Asia are experiencing shortages of staff, disruptions of diagnostics treatment and surveillance systems are collapsing.” ; looking beyond the next four years, if aid funding is not restored, “we see the AIDS pandemic… resurging globally”, growing in Eastern Europe and Latin America ; “We’ll see it come back, and we’ll see people die the way we saw them in the ’90s and in the 2000s.”

a3559.speaker: Winnie Byanyima, UNAIDS executive director
a3559.name: Winnie Byanyima
a3559.title: UNAIDS executive director
a3559.speech: Hailed US leadership in the fight against AIDS as “the greatest acts of humanity in global health” and highlighted the US anti-HIV initiative PEPFAR, which is considered one of the world’s most successful public health efforts, having saved an estimated 26 million lives over two decades.

a3559.speaker: Winnie Byanyima, UNAIDS executive director
a3559.name: Winnie Byanyima
a3559.title: UNAIDS executive director
a3559.speech: Said that thanks to US innovations the world is “at the cusp of another revolution in prevention treatment”, pointing to a new drug called lenacapavir developed by Gilead, and said tests were under way towards providing it as a single injection per year: “That is almost like a flu vaccine. If this could be rolled out ambitiously … we could cut down new infections to close to zero. We could see the end of AIDS.”

a3559.speaker: Winnie Byanyima, UNAIDS executive director
a3559.name: Winnie Byanyima
a3559.title: UNAIDS executive director
a3559.speech: Appealed to the “deal-maker” Trump directly, insisting that rescuing the global HIV response was “an amazing deal”: lenacapavir is able to “make profits for Gilead, to create good jobs for Americans and to save lives”; she suggested that when PEPFAR is brought back online, UNAIDS could work with the United States and other donors to help low-income countries become self-sufficient in the fight against HIV.

a3743.speaker: Rigathi Gachagua, Kenya's former Deputy President and leader of the Democracy for the Citizens Party (DCP)
a3743.name: Rigathi Gachagua
a3743.title: Kenya's former Deputy President and leader of the Democracy for the Citizens Party (DCP)
a3743.speech: Has accused President William Ruto of supplying weapons to the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) in Sudan; alleges that these weapons have been used by the RSF in attacks that have killed women and children; claims that President Ruto and RSF leader Hemeti have business ties; asserted that President William Ruto's administration has ties to terrorist organisations; has also connected the funding of Sudan's Rapid Support Forces to the head of state.

a3743.speaker: Rigathi Gachagua, Kenya's former Deputy President and leader of the Democracy for the Citizens Party (DCP)
a3743.name: Rigathi Gachagua
a3743.title: Kenya's former Deputy President and leader of the Democracy for the Citizens Party (DCP)
a3743.speech: Claimed that Ruto met with three Al-Shabaab militia members at night to talk “business” during his current U.S. tour; declared that he is prepared to assist the U.S. government in investigating Kenya's activities with Al-Shabaab and RSF.

a3743.speaker: Rigathi Gachagua, Kenya's former Deputy President and leader of the Democracy for the Citizens Party (DCP)
a3743.name: Rigathi Gachagua
a3743.title: Kenya's former Deputy President and leader of the Democracy for the Citizens Party (DCP)
a3743.speech: On the investigations: “We can not help in any investigations because the Kenyan government has not initiated any investigations against William Ruto. The people who have initiated the investigation are the American Senate, so if there is a need for us to help in investigations, we will help the American Senate, not the Kenyan government” ; said Kenya is unable to conduct an impartial investigation of Ruto since police officers report to him; warned Kithure Kindiki, his replacement, against what he termed as “selling fear to him.”

a3743.speaker: Kenyan diaspora media reports
a3743.name: Kenyan diaspora media reports
a3743.speech: According to Kenyan diaspora media reports, Gachagua maintains that he owes no explanation to the Kenyan government over the terrorism allegations.

a3743.speaker: Kithure Kindiki, Deputy President, and Kipchumba Murkomen, Interior Cabinet Secretary
a3743.name: Kithure Kindiki
a3743.title: Deputy President, and Kipchumba Murkomen, Interior Cabinet Secretary
a3743.speech: Took note of the comments and insisted that Gachagua make a statement to the police upon his return to Kenya.

a3881.speaker: Right to Care research study led by Prof Cindy Firnhaber (funded by PEPFAR through USAID)
a3881.name: Right to Care research study led by Prof Cindy Firnhaber (funded by PEPFAR through USAID)
a3881.speech: The research, which involved 166 HIV positive women attending Right to Care's Themba Lethu Clinic at Helen Joseph Hospital, "had extremely promising results and indicated that at six months LEEP does a better job than cryotherapy but at 12 months, the effectiveness of LEEP and cryotherapy are not statistically different."

a3881.speaker: Professor Cindy Firnhaber, lead investigator at Right to Care
a3881.name: Professor Cindy Firnhaber
a3881.title: lead investigator at Right to Care
a3881.speech: "Despite cryotherapy taking somewhat longer to be effective, this provides an alternative treatment for cervical abnormalities which can be done in a local clinic. This avoids the need for the woman to travel and also expands much-needed access to treatment," Firnhaber explains.

a3881.speaker: Professor Cindy Firnhaber, lead investigator at Right to Care
a3881.name: Professor Cindy Firnhaber
a3881.title: lead investigator at Right to Care
a3881.speech: On the GeneXpert HPV testing tool, which performed as well as laboratory tests in a comparison involving 1163 patients: "This is particularly good news for those who do not live near the major laboratories," Firnhaber comments.

a3882.speaker: Josep Borrell, High Representative of the European Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy / Vice-President of the European Commission
a3882.name: Josep Borrell
a3882.title: High Representative of the European Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy / Vice-President of the European Commission
a3882.speech: On the purpose of his visit to Mozambique: "Last week I was in Mozambique, a country where EU support plays a significant [role] including through one of the largest recipients of EU support and host to one of our EU military training missions. My visit aimed to show that the EU does not forget crises in other parts of the world, despite facing the worst threat to European security since the end of World War II with the war of aggression against Ukraine. Mozambique's fight against terrorism is one of these security crises that we help to tackle using all EU instruments." ; "In Europe, we are very focused on Russia's aggression against Ukraine and its implications for European security. But other crises and global problems do not stop... We need more than ever to continue to work with our partners around the globe to defend the rules-based order and to keep up our work on global challenges. For this purpose, the EU's close partnership with Africa is crucial."

a3882.speaker: Josep Borrell, EU High Representative/Vice-President
a3882.name: Josep Borrell
a3882.title: EU High Representative/Vice-President
a3882.speech: On the EU training mission and support to SAMIM: "The EUTM Mozambique, launched in November 2021, is a key element in the EU's commitment to help Mozambique's fight against this terrorism. Over the next two years, it will train 11 units of the Mozambican army (commandos and marines) that will be part of a future Quick Reaction Force... This mission is now fully operational, having already trained 600 soldiers." ; "during my visit, I announced the EU decision to provide EUR 15 million to this mission in addition to the EUR 89 million of EPF support. It is the first time ever that we train people while in parallel providing them with equipment. In the coming weeks, I hope that our member states will also agree on my proposal to support the Rwandese military mission that has been decisive to improve the situation in Cabo Delgado."

a3882.speaker: Josep Borrell, EU High Representative/Vice-President
a3882.name: Josep Borrell
a3882.title: EU High Representative/Vice-President
a3882.speech: On winning the peace as well as the war: "But we know that you cannot win a war against terror with soldiers and weapons only. To win this kind of war, one needs to win the peace as well. This is why we work closely with the Government of Mozambique to cover the full spectrum of humanitarian, development, security and peace-building actions. In parallel to our security support, we focus on education, access to water and sanitation, energy, nutrition and climate change. This includes a package of EUR 428 million for the period 2021-2024, in addition to around EUR 36 million of humanitarian assistance (mainly to Cabo Delgado since 2021)."

a3882.speaker: Journalists in Mozambique
a3882.name: Journalists in Mozambique
a3882.speech: "Some journalists in Mozambique have asked me whether our support to the fight against terrorism in Cabo Delgado is linked to the gas reserves in this region."

a3882.speaker: Josep Borrell, EU High Representative/Vice-President
a3882.name: Josep Borrell
a3882.title: EU High Representative/Vice-President
a3882.speech: Answering whether EU support is linked to Cabo Delgado's gas reserves: "My answer was clear: the gas discoveries in Mozambique should benefit the Mozambican people first and foremost, while they can also help to tackle the global energy crisis and energy demand. But that is not the primary reason of our engagement in Mozambique. The security of Europe starts in places that can be sometimes thousands of kilometres away... We need to help avoid that kind of large scale destabilization happening in another place on the continent. This is why we support the efforts of Mozambique in Cabo Delgado."

a3882.speaker: Josep Borrell, EU High Representative/Vice-President
a3882.name: Josep Borrell
a3882.title: EU High Representative/Vice-President
a3882.speech: On multilateralism: "I discussed these issues with the President of Mozambique as well as the Foreign Affairs and Defence Ministers. In addition, we focused on how to strengthen our partnership on the international stage in the context of Mozambique's election as a non-permanent member of the UN Security Council as of next year. Both Mozambique and the EU know that multilateralism needs to be strengthened at a moment when Russia is sending shockwaves around the world by tearing down basis principles of the rules-based order."

a4007.speaker: Minority in Parliament (Ghana)
a4007.name: Minority in Parliament (Ghana)
a4007.speech: At an emergency news conference on Tuesday, August 6, 2024, called on President Akufo-Addo to immediately halt the payment of US$34.9 million to Service Ghana Auto Group Limited (SGAGL), describing the deal as scandalous, unconscionable, a sweetheart deal, and a family affair concerning ambulance spare parts; demanded that the President instruct his Chief of Staff, Frema Opare, to desist from pressuring the Ministers of Health and Finance to make unlawful payments to SGAGL; and urged the Office of the Special Prosecutor to expedite investigations and prosecute all individuals involved in the US$34.9 million ambulance spare parts deal.

a4007.speaker: Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa, Chairman of the Assurances Committee (MP)
a4007.name: Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa
a4007.title: Chairman of the Assurances Committee (MP)
a4007.speech: Responded to what he called “a preposterous and most offensive statement from the discredited Service Ghana Auto Group Limited”: “This ill-advised strategy to use naked threats to prevent parliamentary scrutiny, media discussions, and the legitimate demand for accountability from patriotic Ghanaians who have every right to know what a colossal US$108 million of our taxes are being used for under this opaque ambulance transaction is a strategy bound to fail” ; condemned the use of threats by SGAGL and their attempt to gag Ghanaians, particularly Members of Parliament and the media, advising SGAGL to “desist from issuing empty and pathetic threats as nothing will stop our democratic and patriotic resolve in the spirit of transparency, probity, and media freedoms — which are all guaranteed under the 1992 Constitution, to demand full accountability in this matter. We cannot be intimidated by their bogus threats.”

a4007.speaker: Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa, Chairman of the Assurances Committee (MP)
a4007.name: Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa
a4007.title: Chairman of the Assurances Committee (MP)
a4007.speech: Noted that SGAGL’s statement deliberately failed to address the politically exposed status of a key director, Stephen Okoro, a close business partner of the President’s daughters, Gyankroma Akufo-Addo and Edwina Akufo-Addo, as demonstrated with official incorporation documents of SFO Initiatives Limited, Goodbox Limited, and Good Grow Limited, and that SGAGL was also silent on Stephen Okoro’s familial ties with the presidential family, having fathered a grandchild of the President with one of his daughters; said politically exposed persons always come under greater scrutiny in the fight against corruption as they can unduly influence procurement processes, abuse due process, and orchestrate unconscionable payment terms in their favour.

a4007.speaker: Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa, Chairman of the Assurances Committee (MP)
a4007.name: Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa
a4007.title: Chairman of the Assurances Committee (MP)
a4007.speech: Mentioned that SGAGL claimed to have participated in a competitive procurement process by the Ministry of Special Development Initiatives from November 15, 2018, as a consortium of seven companies, but said records at the Registrar of Companies reveal that Service Ghana Auto Group Limited was incorporated much later, on April 24, 2020; said claims by SGAGL that it is a consortium leveraging the expertise and resources of its companies in the procurement of ambulances are laughable and ridiculous, since at least five of the seven companies were hurriedly incorporated between April and September 2017 and none had any expertise or track record in procuring and servicing ambulances ; added: “Service Ghana Auto Group Limited peddled another blatant falsehood when it claimed that companies in its so-called consortium put in a bid at US$133,000 per ambulance.”

a4007.speaker: Registrar of Companies (incorporation records)
a4007.name: Registrar of Companies (incorporation records)
a4007.speech: Records reveal that Service Ghana Auto Group Limited was incorporated on April 24, 2020, and show that BEFT Engineering was incorporated on April 20, 2017, primarily to carry out construction, renovation, civil engineering works, and electrical engineering works; Elok Consult on July 25, 2017, to carry out management consultancy, civil works, roads, and building construction; and Prestige Era Company Limited on April 19, 2017, to carry out general supply, road, and building construction, oil and gas product dealing, and transport and haulage.

a4007.speaker: Auditor-General (Ghana)
a4007.name: Auditor-General (Ghana)
a4007.speech: Exposed SGAGL for using staff of the National Ambulance Service for their maintenance contract.

a4030.speaker: Facinet Sylla, Guinean Minister of Economy and Finance
a4030.name: Facinet Sylla
a4030.title: Guinean Minister of Economy and Finance
a4030.speech: Recalled that several regional and global factors have upset economic balances, citing in particular the surge in security spending in West Africa, climate shocks and the decline in foreign aid ; "At the national level, the Guinean State has had to cope with unforeseen social expenditures, while continuing the major infrastructure works linked to the Simandou mining project, the engine of the 'Simandou 2040' programme."

a4030.speaker: Facinet Sylla, Guinean Minister of Economy and Finance
a4030.name: Facinet Sylla
a4030.title: Guinean Minister of Economy and Finance
a4030.speech: Also underlined the government's commitments in favour of a return to constitutional order, with the referendum of 21 September 2025 and the preparation of the coming elections.

a4030.speaker: Facinet Sylla, Guinean Minister of Economy and Finance
a4030.name: Facinet Sylla
a4030.title: Guinean Minister of Economy and Finance
a4030.speech: Said revenue forecasts rise from 35,073.41 billion to 43,067 billion Guinean francs, an increase of 22.4% over the initial 2025 finance law: "This increase is mainly driven by the rise in customs receipts (+46%) and the growth of tax receipts (+11.5%). The tax burden now stands at 15.6% of GDP, against 12% previously. On the spending side, expenditures reach 59,394 billion Guinean francs, up 22.8%, driven notably by public investment (+30%)." ; "Despite everything we have had to spend, we have been able to contain current expenditure at a reasonable rate," insisting on budgetary rigour and transparency in the management of public finances.

a4030.speaker: Facinet Sylla, Guinean Minister of Economy and Finance
a4030.name: Facinet Sylla
a4030.title: Guinean Minister of Economy and Finance
a4030.speech: Presented two emblematic measures of the amending finance law: "The VAT exemption and the reduction of customs duties on new vehicles and their accessories. The objective: to encourage the renewal of the vehicle fleet, reduce road accidents and limit fraud on imports." ; "Why should this privilege be reserved for a small elite? Every Guinean should be able to drive a new vehicle," while underlining the VAT exemption on certain electrical equipment and materials, to fight domestic fires caused by poor-quality equipment.

a4030.speaker: Facinet Sylla, Guinean Minister of Economy and Finance
a4030.name: Facinet Sylla
a4030.title: Guinean Minister of Economy and Finance
a4030.speech: Judged the budget deficit of 4% of GDP (against 3.1% initially forecast) "realistic and transparent," and insisted on the government's determination to maintain fiscal sustainability while prioritising investments with a strong social and economic impact.

a4030.speaker: Facinet Sylla, Guinean Minister of Economy and Finance
a4030.name: Facinet Sylla
a4030.title: Guinean Minister of Economy and Finance
a4030.speech: "We must build a more resilient, more equitable economy geared towards sustainable development," he concluded, before calling on the councillors to support this project "in the service of national ambitions."

a4163.speaker: Atupele Muluzi, United Democratic Front (UDF) leader
a4163.name: Atupele Muluzi
a4163.title: United Democratic Front (UDF) leader
a4163.speech: Raised alarm over what he describes as a growing threat to democracy in Malawi, warning that the country is on a dangerous path toward autocratic rule and internal decay; told fellow leaders at the Platform for African Democrats (PAD) conference in Angola that Malawi is experiencing a rollback of democratic principles amid rising global instability and weakening international cooperation: “We are witnessing a dangerous shift: a retreat from the principles that have long underpinned democratic governance. Truth itself has become a casualty, with disinformation distorting the foundations of informed political discourse.” ; Pointed to the consolidation of power by autocratic regimes across the continent, adding that such trends have emboldened leaders who undermine democracy through coercion rather than consent ; Accused several African governments of falling prey to kleptocracy, describing them as “government by the corrupt, for the corrupt,” where leaders prioritize personal enrichment over public service.

a4163.speaker: Atupele Muluzi, United Democratic Front (UDF) leader
a4163.name: Atupele Muluzi
a4163.title: United Democratic Front (UDF) leader
a4163.speech: Accused the current administration of using undemocratic tactics to cling to power: “The current administration has failed to deliver on its economic and social promises. Facing near-certain electoral defeat, it is resorting to undemocratic means to maintain control” ; urged Malawians to resist any attempts to subvert democratic norms and called on Malawians to speak with a united voice to defend the country’s democracy: “This is our moment to stand firm for democracy. We cannot allow our democracy to be stolen.”

a4163.speaker: Atupele Muluzi, United Democratic Front (UDF) leader
a4163.name: Atupele Muluzi
a4163.title: United Democratic Front (UDF) leader
a4163.speech: Highlighted the impact of shrinking international support, citing the scaling back of donor agencies such as USAID, and warned that Africa is being left to tackle economic stagnation, agricultural insecurity, corruption, and poor governance largely on its own: “Yet, this is precisely when we need greater collaboration to tackle Africa’s pressing challenges.”

a4163.speaker: Malawi government officials
a4163.name: Malawi government officials
a4163.speech: Did not immediately respond to Muluzi’s claims.

a4584.speaker: United Nations (UN)
a4584.name: United Nations (UN)
a4584.speech: According to the UN, the increase in the number of deaths in 2024 was caused by the conflicts in the Gaza Strip, where 181 humanitarian workers lost their lives; the majority of these killings in 2024 were perpetrated by state agents, and the majority of those killed were local staff, attacked on duty or in the homes where they lived; the United Nations indicated that last year 308 humanitarian workers were injured, 125 were kidnapped and 45 were detained.

a4584.speaker: United Nations (UN)
a4584.name: United Nations (UN)
a4584.speech: Reiterates that attacks against humanitarian workers constitute violations of international humanitarian law and directly affect the livelihoods on which millions of people trapped in war or disaster zones depend.

a4584.speaker: Aid Worker Security Database (provisional data)
a4584.name: Aid Worker Security Database (provisional data)
a4584.speech: Provisional figures in the database of the Aid Worker Security body show that, as of 14 August, 265 humanitarian workers have been killed since the beginning of 2025.

a4584.speaker: Tom Fletcher, UN Under-Secretary-General for Humanitarian Affairs
a4584.name: Tom Fletcher
a4584.title: UN Under-Secretary-General for Humanitarian Affairs
a4584.speech: "A single attack against a humanitarian colleague (staff member) is an attack on all of us and on those we serve" ; said that impunity for attacks against humanitarian workers constitutes a "shameful expression of international inaction and apathy" ; called for more protection and asked that "justice be done."

a4584.speaker: World Health Organization (WHO)
a4584.name: World Health Organization (WHO)
a4584.speech: Announced that it had recorded, last year, more than 800 attacks against health services in 16 territories, resulting in the deaths of more than 1,100 medical professionals and patients.

a4739.speaker: Dr Konan Diby (present at the workshop, Centre national de recherche agronomique / Ministry of Agriculture training session)
a4739.name: Dr Konan Diby (present at the workshop
a4739.title: Centre national de recherche agronomique / Ministry of Agriculture training session)
a4739.speech: Stated that this training session was aimed at strengthening the capacities of multiplier producers in the proper management of cassava woodlots (parcs à bois); more specifically, that it sought to make participants aware of the identification of cassava varieties, seed production, pest management (weeds, diseases and pests), as well as the establishment and monitoring of a woodlot.

a4774.speaker: Namibian Statistics Agency (NSA)
a4774.name: Namibian Statistics Agency (NSA)
a4774.speech: Indicated the economy's size in the third quarter of 2024 reached N$61.6 billion, marking an increase of N$5.3 billion compared to the N$56.3 billion recorded in the third quarter of 2023.

a4774.speaker: Mirijam Shihepo, NSA spokesperson
a4774.name: Mirijam Shihepo
a4774.title: NSA spokesperson
a4774.speech: Noted, “In real terms, the domestic economy grew by 2.8% during the third quarter of 2024 compared to 3.1% growth registered in the parallel quarter of 2022.”

a4793.speaker: Fr Process Kiocha, diaspora returnee and Parochial Vicar for the Diocese of Columbus, United States
a4793.name: Fr Process Kiocha
a4793.title: diaspora returnee and Parochial Vicar for the Diocese of Columbus, United States
a4793.speech: Shared his motivation for the renovation project with his colleagues: "The return to Mrawi Primary School and the investment in its renovation reflects my deep desire to give back to my community. It's a testament to the power of individuals who are able and willing to help shape the future of education."

a4793.speaker: Fr Process Kiocha, diaspora returnee and Parochial Vicar for the Diocese of Columbus, United States
a4793.name: Fr Process Kiocha
a4793.title: diaspora returnee and Parochial Vicar for the Diocese of Columbus, United States
a4793.speech: "I reached out to my friends and the support poured in. I began collecting small contributions from ordinary people and over time, we raised over 138 million Tanzanian shillings" ; added that the total cost to complete the project will exceed 243m/-.

a4793.speaker: Fr Process Kiocha, diaspora returnee and Parochial Vicar for the Diocese of Columbus, United States
a4793.name: Fr Process Kiocha
a4793.title: diaspora returnee and Parochial Vicar for the Diocese of Columbus, United States
a4793.speech: Acknowledging the vital support of Ms Shirley Tropea, a 90-year-old mother of five from Massillon, Ohio, he reflected: "Ms Tropea first joined me in 2012 and returned in 2013 and 2014. Together, we began supporting the education of several children, many of whom reached high school, with a few even advancing to university. I distinctly remember a time when we were helping 18 children who were struggling, providing them with uniforms, tuition fees, pocket money and other essentials." ; "Little by little, we also began working on improving the playground and today, we have made significant progress. Last year we celebrated two graduates: One from Mlama High School in Moshi, who completed his Form Four studies and another from Mwenge University in Moshi, who earned his university degree".

a4793.speaker: Deacon Reed Hauser, Permanent Deacon, Our Lady Queen of Apostles, Diocese of Columbus, Ohio
a4793.name: Deacon Reed Hauser
a4793.title: Permanent Deacon, Our Lady Queen of Apostles, Diocese of Columbus, Ohio
a4793.speech: Emphasised the importance of support systems, both from the home and the community, to ensure students can succeed; spoke about the long-term impact of the renovations, reminding the community that the efforts to improve the school would benefit future generations, saying the impact was seen in the students' eyes.

a4793.speaker: Deacon Reed Hauser, Permanent Deacon, Our Lady Queen of Apostles, Diocese of Columbus, Ohio
a4793.name: Deacon Reed Hauser
a4793.title: Permanent Deacon, Our Lady Queen of Apostles, Diocese of Columbus, Ohio
a4793.speech: "Fr Kiocha's initiative resonated with me on many levels," adding the opportunity to give back to the community that helped shape him as a young man felt like a natural extension of the work we do here living our faith by helping others in need, wherever they are.

a4793.speaker: Mr Bob Lagnese, parishioner of Our Lady Queen of Apostles, Diocese of Columbus, Ohio
a4793.name: Mr Bob Lagnese
a4793.title: parishioner of Our Lady Queen of Apostles, Diocese of Columbus, Ohio
a4793.speech: "It's inspiring to see these children so eager to learn. You can feel the energy shift when they see their school being transformed. They understand that this isn't just about new classrooms but it's about new opportunities" ; "Education is the foundation of everything. By helping to improve this school, we are giving these children the tools to build better lives for themselves and their communities."

a4793.speaker: Mr Denis Tarimo, Education Officer for the Hai Eastern Division
a4793.name: Mr Denis Tarimo
a4793.title: Education Officer for the Hai Eastern Division
a4793.speech: Emphasised the crucial role of collaboration between the government, local communities and development partners in shaping the nation's future through education; highlighted that while the government plays a key role in managing numerous schools, its ability to address the needs of all schools can be limited due to resource constraints: "There are many schools that rely on government support, but due to the sheer number of these institutions it is not always easy for the government to address all their needs" ; said this is where the involvement of the community and external stakeholders becomes crucial.

a4793.speaker: Mr Denis Tarimo, Education Officer for the Hai Eastern Division
a4793.name: Mr Denis Tarimo
a4793.title: Education Officer for the Hai Eastern Division
a4793.speech: Expressed his gratitude for the work done at Mrawi Primary School, emphasising that such contributions serve as a powerful example of how communities can come together to support education: "The renovations done by our community members are a great source of encouragement to the government. We recognise and greatly appreciate the substantial contributions made by the community towards improving the education sector" ; commended the efforts of Fr Kiocha and his team for creating a lasting legacy: "The support provided by Fr Kiocha and his team has created a lasting legacy. The children here will forever remember this act of generosity, and as they grow older, they will be inspired to give back to their communities."

a4793.speaker: Mr Ludovick Makundi, Headmaster of Mrawi Primary School
a4793.name: Mr Ludovick Makundi
a4793.title: Headmaster of Mrawi Primary School
a4793.speech: Expressed his deep gratitude for the renovations, noting that the improvements had significantly boosted the school's capacity to provide quality education: "The support from Fr Kiocha and his team along with the continued involvement of the local community has positioned us to provide quality education for generations to come" ; "Before the renovations we only enrolled children from Mrawi village. Now, we are seeing children from neighbouring villages expressing interest in studying here" ; said the time spent with teachers, communities and students created an enduring connection between the people of Mrawi and the supporters from Our Lady Queen of Apostles ; "Fr Kiocha, Deacon Hauser and Mr Lagnese's involvement has not only transformed Mrawi Primary School physically but has also sparked a renewed sense of pride and possibility within the community. Their actions have shown that when people come together, no matter where you come from you can make a meaningful impact when you work together for a common cause."

a4793.speaker: Fransiska Msoka and Glory Sangawe, students at Mrawi Primary School
a4793.name: Fransiska Msoka and Glory Sangawe
a4793.title: students at Mrawi Primary School
a4793.speech: Shared that they are thrilled to study in the new classrooms, explaining that before the renovation, the old classrooms were uncomfortable, making it difficult to concentrate, and that now they find it much easier to focus on their studies.

a4793.speaker: Melkior Mushi, student at Mrawi Primary School
a4793.name: Melkior Mushi
a4793.title: student at Mrawi Primary School
a4793.speech: Highlighted that the new toilets and multipurpose hall have made the school feel more modern: "We now have a space where we can gather for meetings and performances", adding that the new facilities are especially beneficial for students with disabilities, particularly the updated provisions in the toilets.

a4795.speaker: Moses Kunkuyu, Malawi Government spokesperson
a4795.name: Moses Kunkuyu
a4795.title: Malawi Government spokesperson
a4795.speech: Has since acknowledged that since the time of Covid, the world is reshaping in many aspects. “Nations will have to re-strategise and realign with objectives that suit their individual aspirations. New friendships and partnerships will be born. With the direction that Malawi has taken in safeguarding its mineral endowment, Malawi will be the most beautiful girl in town very soon.” ; “We believe the usual avenues of providing counsel to government will still be utilised so that we maximise gains by engaging in conversations where ‘tough decisions’ can be elaborated.” ; He expressed hope that the issue of perpetual dependence on aid would become history.

a4795.speaker: Keir Starmer, UK Prime Minister
a4795.name: Keir Starmer
a4795.title: UK Prime Minister
a4795.speech: Said his government would not pretend that cutting off aid was going to be easy.

a4795.speaker: Anneliese Dodds, UK International Development Minister
a4795.name: Anneliese Dodds
a4795.title: UK International Development Minister
a4795.speech: Resigned in protest, accusing Starmer of undermining global poverty alleviation efforts and strengthening the influence of Russia and China in Africa.

a4795.speaker: Humanitarian groups and economists
a4795.name: Humanitarian groups and economists
a4795.speech: Have concurred with Dodds, warning of severe consequences for vulnerable populations in Malawi, which they say rely heavily on donor funding for critical development projects.

a4795.speaker: Habiba Osman, Malawi Human Rights Commission Executive Secretary
a4795.name: Habiba Osman
a4795.title: Malawi Human Rights Commission Executive Secretary
a4795.speech: Said the potential cut meant the Malawi Government needed to explore alternative funding sources. She said the transition may not be smooth, such that vulnerable populations were likely to bear the brunt of such cuts. She said Malawi relies heavily on foreign aid to run critical sectors such as health, education and general infrastructure development projects, and even relied on foreign assistance to run national elections. ; “A cut in UK funding could stall, or even halt, ongoing development projects. Programmes [that are] supporting poverty reduction, water and sanitation, and food security efforts may experience financial shortfalls.”

a4795.speaker: Velli Nyirongo, Economist
a4795.name: Velli Nyirongo
a4795.title: Economist
a4795.speech: Concurred with Osman, saying the UK’s decision to scale down aid to Malawi was a concerning development, particularly as the specifics of how much funding would be cut remained unclear. “The UK has long been a key donor to Malawi, but shifting global priorities suggest that its focus is changing. This raises significant challenges for Malawi, as crucial sectors such as climate change, maternal health and education may face critical funding shortfalls.”

a4795.speaker: Gift Trapence, Human Rights Defenders Coalition Chairperson
a4795.name: Gift Trapence
a4795.title: Human Rights Defenders Coalition Chairperson
a4795.speech: Said Malawi risked facing increased poverty levels and associated consequences. “The UK has been a key donor in Malawi’s health sector, particularly in fighting malaria, HIV and Aids and maternal health. Reduced funding could lead to shortages of essential medicines and medical supplies.” ; “Social protection programmes that are benefitting vulnerable populations, including children and the elderly, may also suffer.”

a4891.speaker: Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Cooperation and Nigeriens Abroad of Niger (communiqué)
a4891.name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs
a4891.title: Cooperation and Nigeriens Abroad of Niger (communiqué)
a4891.speech: states that the Government of the Republic of Niger never issued an appeal for international humanitarian aid following the floods, still less to the European Union, and that the Nigerien Government had sovereignly decided to cover the flood damage from its own funds; that the announcement of this unsolicited aid appeared on social media two weeks before the Nigerien authorities were officially informed, contrary to diplomatic practice repeatedly recalled by circular Notes Verbales stating that the Ministry is the sole interlocutor of diplomatic missions; that, worse, the aid was delivered to the regions through NGOs chosen by the EU Delegation in Niamey in total opacity; that this attitude of contempt led the Minister of Foreign Affairs to summon EU Ambassador Salvador Pinto Da França on 14 October 2024 and instruct him to end the ongoing operations; that two months later the Government bitterly noted that unauthorised operations were continuing; that in view of this stubbornness the Government concluded that collaboration with Ambassador Salvador Pinto Da França is no longer possible and officially requested his recall and replacement as soon as possible; that the recall of the ambassador is therefore an initiative of the Nigerien Government and not of the European Union; and reaffirming Niger’s commitment to work with all countries and international organisations devoted to peace and justice, with respect for its sovereignty, its dignity, its national strategic choices and the interests of its populations.

a4891.speaker: European Union (communiqué of 23 November 2024)
a4891.name: European Union (communiqué of 23 November 2024)
a4891.speech: expressed its disagreement with the reasons invoked by Niger regarding the management of humanitarian aid to flood victims, and recalled its Ambassador to Niger for consultations.

a4970.speaker: Elon Musk, American businessman tasked by Donald Trump with cleaning house within the federal government
a4970.name: Elon Musk
a4970.title: American businessman tasked by Donald Trump with cleaning house within the federal government
a4970.speech: Announced the closure of the US Agency for International Development (USAID), with all its offices to close no later than Friday 7 February 2025; accused the agency of being a "criminal organisation" and said it was "time for it to die."

a4970.speaker: Donald Trump, US President (presidential executive order of 25 January 2025)
a4970.name: Donald Trump
a4970.title: US President (presidential executive order of 25 January 2025)
a4970.speech: Issued a presidential executive order on 25 January 2025 freezing American foreign aid for 90 days, with the exception of Israel, Egypt and emergency food aid; supported the decision to close USAID.

a4987.speaker: Johannes Mururani, participant in the Commitment Walk
a4987.name: Johannes Mururani
a4987.title: participant in the Commitment Walk
a4987.speech: told the group he was a violent man until he attended a male engagement program on gender norms under the USAID Reach Namibia Project, and is now adamant about creating a safe environment: "Imagine a world where boys and girls can walk safely to school without fear of violence. A world where women can make decisions about their health and bodies without coercion. A world where men and women stand together as equals, united in the fight against gender-based violence and HIV."

a4987.speaker: Katamba Nanyemba, Project Coordinator of the Reach Namibia Project
a4987.name: Katamba Nanyemba
a4987.title: Project Coordinator of the Reach Namibia Project
a4987.speech: says the link between gender-based violence and HIV is well documented: "It shows us that survivors of violence have often limited control over their sexual health, face power imbalances that prevent them from negotiating safer sex, and fear stigma that deters them from accessing critical services."

a4987.speaker: Bonifatius Wakudumo, Kavango East Governor
a4987.name: Bonifatius Wakudumo
a4987.title: Kavango East Governor
a4987.speech: told the group that it is their duty as men to educate themselves and others about GBV, its root causes, and its impact on individuals: "It is believed that five in six men are not abusers. But where are they? Can they stand up and be counted? Can the one in six who are abusers change their ways? Can we raise a new generation based on equality? Change is not easy, and it does not happen overnight. But every step we take today is a step toward building a safer and more equitable future. Let us be unwavering in our commitment and courageous in our actions."

a5366.speaker: Bassirou Diomaye Faye, President of Senegal
a5366.name: Bassirou Diomaye Faye
a5366.title: President of Senegal
a5366.speech: "Mr President, I would first like to thank you for all the marks of hospitality and the warm welcome extended to me here on the African soil of Benin, and to my delegation, and also to thank you for the quality of the exchanges we have had, with a wide-ranging tour of all the subjects of bilateral cooperation, but also and above all on the multilateral level, with the challenges confronting our sub-region today." ; "I will end my remarks by reiterating my thanks to President Talon and to the brotherly Beninese people, wishing you and all Beninese men and women a happy independence day in advance. Thank you very much."

a5366.speaker: Bassirou Diomaye Faye, President of Senegal
a5366.name: Bassirou Diomaye Faye
a5366.title: President of Senegal
a5366.speech: "As soon as I took office, I had undertaken a tour to pay my respects to my brother heads of State, and Benin figured very prominently in the calendar of those visits. Unfortunately, scheduling constraints and constraints external and internal to Senegal, but also scheduling constraints on your side, did not allow the visit to take place when I wanted it to, but I had nevertheless insisted on calling you on the telephone and telling you how impatient I was to meet you." ; "That telephone call obviously triggered much friendship between us, because you picked up that telephone with great warmth. We had at that moment a very fruitful discussion, which we have continued on the rare occasions when we have met."

a5366.speaker: Bassirou Diomaye Faye, President of Senegal
a5366.name: Bassirou Diomaye Faye
a5366.title: President of Senegal
a5366.speech: "We of course discussed the relations of friendship and cooperation between Benin [and Senegal], which are cordial and very convivial, even though both of us noted that today, given the quality of the relationship, we can do much more and much better in terms of trade."

a5366.speaker: Bassirou Diomaye Faye, President of Senegal
a5366.name: Bassirou Diomaye Faye
a5366.title: President of Senegal
a5366.speech: "We also spoke about the situation of the sub-region, both at the ECOWAS level and at the UEMOA level, but also about the security situation in the sub-region, which is very worrying. I took the opportunity to express all my solidarity with President Talon and with the brotherly Beninese people regarding the painful events that have occurred in the framework of the fight against terrorism, and to convey to him Senegal's support in those moments, by which we too are just as affected." ; "We also spoke about UEMOA which, as we know, is going through a somewhat difficult situation that we must address quickly, and President Talon and I agreed, in the very near future, to undertake steps to work on revitalising the organisation, to give it a new breath, of course with the support of the other fellow member States of the union." ; "As for ECOWAS, we have not long ago returned from a summit which was nonetheless a moment of constructive exchange among heads of State, and I recalled a short while ago to President Talon all the importance of the subjects we discussed and the challenges facing the organisation, which must, as in the case of UEMOA as well, obviously reform itself in order to be able to take on the challenges of our era."

a5719.speaker: Study by a UK team
a5719.name: Study by a UK team
a5719.speech: Revealed high levels of lead in locally-produced paints, prompting the EPA to take swift action.

a5719.speaker: Rafael Ngumbu, Manager of Environmental Research and Radiations Safety at the EPA
a5719.name: Rafael Ngumbu
a5719.title: Manager of Environmental Research and Radiations Safety at the EPA
a5719.speech: Explains that consultations started in 2019, leading to the development of the regulation and formation of a technical working group.

a5719.speaker: Dr. Emmanuel King Urey Yarkpawolo, EPA Executive Director
a5719.name: Dr. Emmanuel King Urey Yarkpawolo
a5719.title: EPA Executive Director
a5719.speech: Speaking during the signing ceremony, emphasized the harmful effects of lead exposure, particularly on children and pregnant women: "Lead poisoning causes irreversible damage to the brain and nervous system, decreases IQ, and increases the risk of behavioral problems." ; Observes that lead in paint is a significant source of exposure, especially as paints decay and release toxic dust and flakes into the environment.

a5719.speaker: Dr. Emmanuel King Urey Yarkpawolo, EPA Executive Director
a5719.name: Dr. Emmanuel King Urey Yarkpawolo
a5719.title: EPA Executive Director
a5719.speech: Extolls the government, NPHIL, and international partners, including the Lead Exposure Elimination Project (LEEP), for their support in drafting and implementing the regulation; assures the public of the EPA's commitment to strict implementation, including testing paint samples, creating awareness, and supporting manufacturers in transitioning to lead-free production.

a5719.speaker: Dr. Dougbeh Chris Nyan, Director General of the National Public Health Institute of Liberia (NPHIL)
a5719.name: Dr. Dougbeh Chris Nyan
a5719.title: Director General of the National Public Health Institute of Liberia (NPHIL)
a5719.speech: Describes the signing as a "historic milestone" and stresses the importance of rigorous enforcement of the regulation: "This is not just another signing ceremony. It's about ensuring that our enforcement teams monitor compliance, especially among manufacturers producing lead-based paints." ; "As President Boakai has said, this will not be business as usual. Implementation and enforcement will be key."

a5719.speaker: Dr. Dougbeh Chris Nyan, Director General of the National Public Health Institute of Liberia (NPHIL)
a5719.name: Dr. Dougbeh Chris Nyan
a5719.title: Director General of the National Public Health Institute of Liberia (NPHIL)
a5719.speech: Highlights the collaboration between EPA and NPHIL as a model for inter-agency cooperation, ensuring that public health and environmental protection are addressed holistically.

a5719.speaker: Jerry Toe, Focal Point for the Lead Paint Regulations
a5719.name: Jerry Toe
a5719.title: Focal Point for the Lead Paint Regulations
a5719.speech: Described the regulations as a major initiative: "This is not just a regulatory milestone but a testament to the collaborative efforts of stakeholders who have worked tirelessly to protect public health," highlighting that lead exposure remains a critical public health challenge in developing countries like Liberia.

a5824.speaker: Amy Berman Jackson, US District Judge (preliminary injunction order)
a5824.name: Amy Berman Jackson
a5824.title: US District Judge (preliminary injunction order)
a5824.speech: "The Court cannot look away or the CFPB will be dissolved and dismantled completely in approximately thirty days, well before this lawsuit has come to its conclusion," the judge wrote in her order ; "If the defendants are not enjoined, they will eliminate the agency before the Court has the opportunity to decide whether the law permits them to do it," Berman Jackson wrote ; "The motion for preliminary injunction to be decided boils down to one question: should the Court take action to preserve the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau now before the case concerning its fate has been resolved? That is an extraordinary step." ; "The Court’s oversight is the only thing holding the defendants back."

a5824.speaker: Amy Berman Jackson, US District Judge (preliminary injunction order)
a5824.name: Amy Berman Jackson
a5824.title: US District Judge (preliminary injunction order)
a5824.speech: Said the case raised questions about the separation of powers under the US Constitution and whether the president had encroached upon "legislative authority" ; "The evidence reveals that: the defendants were in fact engaged in a concerted, expedited effort to shut the agency down entirely when the motion for injunctive relief was filed," she wrote ; "While the President is free to propose legislation to Congress to accomplish this aim, the defendants are not free to eliminate an agency created by statute on their own, and certainly not before the Court has had an opportunity to rule on the merits of the plaintiffs’ challenge."

a5824.speaker: Amy Berman Jackson, US District Judge (preliminary injunction order)
a5824.name: Amy Berman Jackson
a5824.title: US District Judge (preliminary injunction order)
a5824.speech: Highlighted what she called "disingenuous" arguments from the Trump administration’s lawyers ; "The Court is left with little confidence that the defense can be trusted to tell the truth about anything," the judge wrote.

a5824.speaker: Amy Berman Jackson, US District Judge (preliminary injunction order)
a5824.name: Amy Berman Jackson
a5824.title: US District Judge (preliminary injunction order)
a5824.speech: On the plaintiff Reverend Eva Steege: "It was her hope to resolve the debt and spare her family that burden after she died," Judge Berman Jackson wrote in her ruling ; "Steege’s fear of leaving her surviving family members saddled with her student loan debt came to pass on March 15, when she died," the judge explained.

a5824.speaker: Plaintiffs (employees, advocates and union representatives, including the National Treasury Employees Union and the NAACP)
a5824.name: Plaintiffs (employees
a5824.title: advocates and union representatives, including the National Treasury Employees Union and the NAACP)
a5824.speech: Requested a preliminary injunction preventing the bureau from being shuttered while court proceedings continue; the judge agreed with the plaintiffs that there was a risk of immediate, irreparable harm, given the speed with which the Trump administration’s efforts have unfolded.

a5824.speaker: Marco Rubio, US Secretary of State
a5824.name: Marco Rubio
a5824.title: US Secretary of State
a5824.speech: Announced he had informed Congress of plans to absorb the US Agency for International Development (USAID) into the State Department, putting its independent functions under executive control.

a5824.speaker: Russell Vought, Director of the Office of Management and Budget
a5824.name: Russell Vought
a5824.title: Director of the Office of Management and Budget
a5824.speech: "The CFPB has been a woke and weaponised agency against disfavoured industries and individuals for a long time. This must end."

a5824.speaker: Elon Musk, Trump adviser and billionaire businessman
a5824.name: Elon Musk
a5824.title: Trump adviser and billionaire businessman
a5824.speech: Called to "delete" the bureau ; "CFPB RIP," he wrote succinctly on February 7, as his Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE) led the dismantling of the organisation.

a5824.speaker: Court complaint (legal filing)
a5824.name: Court complaint (legal filing)
a5824.speech: Steege is in hospice care at the time, according to the complaint.

a5906.speaker: Dini Abdallah Omar, Secretary General of the Ministry of Urban Planning, Environment and Tourism (MUET) of Djibouti
a5906.name: Dini Abdallah Omar
a5906.title: Secretary General of the Ministry of Urban Planning, Environment and Tourism (MUET) of Djibouti
a5906.speech: Recalled in his opening speech that in 2020, marking the 35th anniversary of the adoption of the Vienna Convention, the International Day for the Preservation of the Ozone Layer has as its theme “Ozone for life: 35 years of ozone layer protection”, and that the theme recalls the essential role of the ozone layer as a filter of the sun's harmful ultraviolet radiation and a shield protecting all life on Earth ; Indicated that for more than three decades the international community has deployed all its efforts to combat ozone-depleting substances.

a5906.speaker: Dini Abdallah Omar, Secretary General of the Ministry of Urban Planning, Environment and Tourism (MUET) of Djibouti
a5906.name: Dini Abdallah Omar
a5906.title: Secretary General of the Ministry of Urban Planning, Environment and Tourism (MUET) of Djibouti
a5906.speech: Detailed that at the national level, since ratification of the legal instruments, Djibouti has undertaken a number of activities in favour of protecting the ozone layer: awareness workshops, regulations on controlling imports of ozone-depleting substances (ODS), training sessions for customs officers on ODS import control and detection techniques, training for refrigeration technicians on good practices and CFC recovery/recycling, distribution of recovery and recycling equipment and toolkits to refrigeration technicians including those in the informal sector, and distribution of ODS identifiers to customs officers.

a5906.speaker: Dini Abdallah Omar, Secretary General of the Ministry of Urban Planning, Environment and Tourism (MUET) of Djibouti
a5906.name: Dini Abdallah Omar
a5906.title: Secretary General of the Ministry of Urban Planning, Environment and Tourism (MUET) of Djibouti
a5906.speech: Urged all actors involved in implementing the ozone layer protection programme – customs officers, economic operators, refrigeration technicians and administration officials – to work together to achieve the objectives of the Vienna Convention and the Montreal Protocol, and invited all Djiboutians to act to protect the ozone layer: “More than ever, we are called upon to adopt a more ecological way of life aimed at preserving our planet from any factor of degradation, in particular emissions of ODS.”

a5912.speaker: John Mutorwa, former Deputy Prime Minister of Namibia
a5912.name: John Mutorwa
a5912.title: former Deputy Prime Minister of Namibia
a5912.speech: Expressed deep gratitude for the assistance, highlighting the importance of international solidarity in times of crisis: “This generous donation from your respective countries, your excellencies, is a true reflection of international solidarity, our shared humanity, and the noble responsibility to help one another in times of crisis.” ; “These contributions have significantly empowered our efforts as a country to assist those in dire need. We extend our sincere and profound gratitude to all our international partners for their unwavering support.”

a5912.speaker: John Mutorwa, former Deputy Prime Minister of Namibia
a5912.name: John Mutorwa
a5912.title: former Deputy Prime Minister of Namibia
a5912.speech: Said that despite the rains across the country over the past few weeks, drought remains a problem; on the vulnerability figures: “These figures include different age groups, from the elderly to parents and children, who experience the harsh reality of hunger and loss of livelihoods. As a caring government, it is our responsibility to attend to the plight of affected citizens.”

a5912.speaker: 2024/25 livelihood vulnerability assessment and analysis, Office of the Prime Minister of Namibia
a5912.name: 2024/25 livelihood vulnerability assessment and analysis
a5912.title: Office of the Prime Minister of Namibia
a5912.speech: Revealed that approximately 1.2 million Namibians – 41% of the population – are currently food insecure.

a5912.speaker: John Mutorwa, former Deputy Prime Minister of Namibia
a5912.name: John Mutorwa
a5912.title: former Deputy Prime Minister of Namibia
a5912.speech: Says the scale of the crisis has outstripped available financial resources, with a funding shortfall of approximately N$600 million needed to sustain relief efforts until June this year, and that support received from international partners has been invaluable.

a5964.speaker: United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA), humanitarian overview of the Sahel
a5964.name: United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA)
a5964.title: humanitarian overview of the Sahel
a5964.speech: “As of 1st December 2024, 5.6 million people in the region were internally displaced, and 2.1 million were refugees”; the UN agency further states that almost 33 million women, children, and men in Burkina Faso, Cameroon’s Far North, Mali, Niger, northeastern Nigeria, and Chad need humanitarian assistance and protection services.

a5964.speaker: Yusuf Tuggar, Nigeria’s Minister of Foreign Affairs
a5964.name: Yusuf Tuggar
a5964.title: Nigeria’s Minister of Foreign Affairs
a5964.speech: Said that while external support in the form of donor funding has been helpful in alleviating the burden on the people of the Sahel, it will ultimately take the effort of domestic governments in the region to find a long-lasting solution and ensure peace and stability.

a5964.speaker: Yusuf Tuggar, Nigeria’s Minister of Foreign Affairs
a5964.name: Yusuf Tuggar
a5964.title: Nigeria’s Minister of Foreign Affairs
a5964.speech: Noted that instability in the Sahel exacerbates insecurity in Nigeria — a country that borders various Sahelian nations such as Niger, Mali, and Chad, which are hotspots for violent extremism — and further stated that the unconstitutional changes of government in Niger, Mali, and Burkina Faso, brought about by military coups that ousted democratically elected governments, further complicate efforts geared towards cooperative security initiatives.

a5964.speaker: Yusuf Tuggar, Nigeria’s Minister of Foreign Affairs
a5964.name: Yusuf Tuggar
a5964.title: Nigeria’s Minister of Foreign Affairs
a5964.speech: Debunked claims about Nigeria’s ECOWAS policy by citing the constitution: “Nigeria’s five foreign policy objectives include the promotion and protection of the national interest, African integration and support for African unity, promotion of international cooperation for peace and mutual respect, respect of international law and treaty obligations, and the promotion of a just world economic order”; and has “engaged diplomatically without pause, proposing personal visits and inviting senior government officials and representatives.”

a5964.speaker: Stakeholders and international affairs commentators
a5964.name: Stakeholders and international affairs commentators
a5964.speech: Often argue that Nigeria need not meddle in, nor concern itself with, the internal affairs of other nations, citing international law and norms as the basis for this assertion.

a5964.speaker: Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria
a5964.name: Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria
a5964.speech: Extols guidelines by which the nation’s foreign policy is to be conceptualised and actualised by every administration, and unequivocally demands international cooperation between Nigeria and its allies to achieve peace and security.

a5964.speaker: Nigeria’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs
a5964.name: Nigeria’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs
a5964.speech: Has expressed its commitment to continued diplomatic relations with Niger, Mali, and Burkina Faso.

a5964.speaker: General Abdourahamane Tchiani, Niger’s military leader
a5964.name: General Abdourahamane Tchiani
a5964.title: Niger’s military leader
a5964.speech: Made agenda-laden accusations alleging Nigeria’s involvement in an international conspiracy with France to destabilise his country.

a6081.speaker: Rudolph Atallah, retired Lieutenant-Colonel, senior deputy director for counterterrorism at the White House National Security Council
a6081.name: Rudolph Atallah
a6081.title: retired Lieutenant-Colonel, senior deputy director for counterterrorism at the White House National Security Council
a6081.speech: Stressed that the United States sees Africa as a partner and wants to work with Mali and the other member countries of the Alliance of Sahel States (AES) ; said the terrorist threat is enormous in West Africa and that Mali is considered the centre of this threat which affects the lives of Malians, recommending that the United States must collaborate with Mali and the other AES countries to find a solution ; “We are just here to offer our help. If it suits Mali, it is free to collaborate with us in order to find a solution to the current situation which is affecting Malians and Mali's economy”, while hoping that Mali and the AES member states can be more stable and prosperous as regards security.

a6081.speaker: Rudolph Atallah, retired Lieutenant-Colonel, senior deputy director for counterterrorism at the White House National Security Council
a6081.name: Rudolph Atallah
a6081.title: retired Lieutenant-Colonel, senior deputy director for counterterrorism at the White House National Security Council
a6081.speech: Concerning the Russian or foreign presence in Mali, thinks that Mali is free to choose with whom to collaborate or work.

a6081.speaker: Rudolph Atallah, retired Lieutenant-Colonel, senior deputy director for counterterrorism at the White House National Security Council
a6081.name: Rudolph Atallah
a6081.title: retired Lieutenant-Colonel, senior deputy director for counterterrorism at the White House National Security Council
a6081.speech: Says he has observed Mali since the year 1997 up to today, and wishes for an internal reconciliation among all Malians; for him, this would facilitate and open the door to American investors who would like to come to Mali.

a6081.speaker: Rudolph Atallah, retired Lieutenant-Colonel, senior deputy director for counterterrorism at the White House National Security Council
a6081.name: Rudolph Atallah
a6081.title: retired Lieutenant-Colonel, senior deputy director for counterterrorism at the White House National Security Council
a6081.speech: Concerning the creation of the AES, said that this decision is that of the member countries of the Confederation and does not depend on the United States; as regards the AES joint force, he finds it logical in order to confront the terrorist threat in this zone, insisting that the AES member states must take care of their populations and see to their security and stability.

a6081.speaker: Rudolph Atallah, retired Lieutenant-Colonel, senior deputy director for counterterrorism at the White House National Security Council (envoy of the Trump administration)
a6081.name: Rudolph Atallah
a6081.title: retired Lieutenant-Colonel, senior deputy director for counterterrorism at the White House National Security Council (envoy of the Trump administration)
a6081.speech: Regarding the United States Agency for International Development (USAID), specifies that this organisation no longer exists.

a6081.speaker: Rudolph Atallah, retired Lieutenant-Colonel, senior deputy director for counterterrorism at the White House National Security Council
a6081.name: Rudolph Atallah
a6081.title: retired Lieutenant-Colonel, senior deputy director for counterterrorism at the White House National Security Council
a6081.speech: On the strategy of the fight against terrorism, revealed with pride that the United States are the best in this field: “We have adequate equipment, knowledge and forces to confront this threat. If Mali decides to work with us, we will know how to confront the terrorist threat in Mali”, while signalling that the method of stabilisation will depend simply on Mali.

a6118.speaker: Atupele Muluzi, United Democratic Front (UDF) presidential candidate
a6118.name: Atupele Muluzi
a6118.title: United Democratic Front (UDF) presidential candidate
a6118.speech: Took aim at arrogant political elites who are already parading themselves as winners, warning them to wait for the people’s verdict at the ballot box — because on voting day they will be shocked, and no rigging or backroom deals will save them; declared that Malawi’s hour of reckoning had come, and that the September 16 General Election would not be business as usual.

a6118.speaker: Atupele Muluzi, United Democratic Front (UDF) presidential candidate
a6118.name: Atupele Muluzi
a6118.title: United Democratic Front (UDF) presidential candidate
a6118.speech: Delivered a blistering critique of the current crop of leaders, accusing them of looting the country dry while parading themselves as champions of development: “Malawi does not need leaders whose only record is corruption, arrogance, and failed promises... This country needs fresh blood, and I am ready to lead that generational reset.”

a6118.speaker: Atupele Muluzi, United Democratic Front (UDF) presidential candidate
a6118.name: Atupele Muluzi
a6118.title: United Democratic Front (UDF) presidential candidate
a6118.speech: Pledged to revive coupon starter packs to give struggling farmers access to inputs while opening the doors to large-scale commercial farming aimed at exports: “We must track our resources. We must digitise. We must move beyond subsistence farming into serious agribusiness. That is how Malawi will grow—not through empty speeches or stolen billions.”

a6118.speaker: Angela Muluzi, wife of Atupele Muluzi
a6118.name: Angela Muluzi
a6118.title: wife of Atupele Muluzi
a6118.speech: Called on Malawians to stop gambling with their future by voting for leaders with dirty hands.

a6118.speaker: Lilian Patel, UDF chairperson
a6118.name: Lilian Patel
a6118.title: UDF chairperson
a6118.speech: Reminded the gathering of the glaring betrayal of Malawi’s women—who make up 51% of the electorate yet remain sidelined in decision-making. She said Atupele’s leadership would mark a turning point, placing women where they belong: at the heart of power.

a6152.speaker: Daniel Chapo, President of the Republic of Mozambique
a6152.name: Daniel Chapo
a6152.title: President of the Republic of Mozambique
a6152.speech: Demands that all individuals involved in financial crimes in the Public Administration be held accountable. Daniel Chapo wants greater strategic coordination and information sharing between the Administrative Court, the bodies of the administration of Justice and of investigation, in order to eliminate barriers in the fight against fraud and corruption.

a6152.speaker: Emilia Moiane, director of the information office (Gabinete de Informacao)
a6152.name: Emilia Moiane
a6152.title: director of the information office (Gabinete de Informacao)
a6152.speech: AIM, the Mozambican news agency, must position itself in the mission of promoting the country's achievements, the consolidation of national unity, national interests, the promotion of democracy and social justice. Those were the words of the director of the information office, Emilia Moiane, presiding over the swearing-in this Wednesday in Maputo of Orlando Gambeta, the new director general of AIM.

a6152.speaker: Producers in Gorongosa
a6152.name: Producers in Gorongosa
a6152.speech: Are calling for the harmonisation of the selling price of bananas. They want them to be sold by the kilogram and not by the bunch.

a6346.speaker: United States government / US Embassy in Juba (press statement on World AIDS Day)
a6346.name: United States government / US Embassy in Juba (press statement on World AIDS Day)
a6346.speech: Announced $42 million for this year to support South Sudan's fight against HIV/AIDS through treatment and prevention, as it encourages the transitional government to use public money to strengthen the health system; underscored that an estimated 160,000 people are living with HIV in the country, with their families and communities bearing the burden of the disease; pointed out its longstanding assistance to South Sudan in combating the epidemic since 2007, providing $367 million in HIV relief through the President's Emergency Plan for AIDS Relief (PEPFAR). “This year alone, PEPFAR is investing $42 million to support over 87% of the 63,000 South Sudanese currently on HIV treatment,” the statement said.

a6346.speaker: United States government / US Embassy in Juba (press statement on World AIDS Day)
a6346.name: United States government / US Embassy in Juba (press statement on World AIDS Day)
a6346.speech: Added that for South Sudan's population to be free from the deadly disease, the government must use national revenue to strengthen its healthcare system. “We urge the transitional government to use public revenue to strengthen the health system through investing in healthcare facilities, training healthcare workers, and ensuring equitable access to quality care for all.” The diplomatic mission said it continues to engage and support civil society organizations advocating for the welfare of people living with the virus, provide essential services, and promote social inclusion.

a6346.speaker: Hussein Abdelbagi, Vice President of South Sudan and Chairperson of the Service Cluster
a6346.name: Hussein Abdelbagi
a6346.title: Vice President of South Sudan and Chairperson of the Service Cluster
a6346.speech: Recently said HIV/AIDs remains a significant public health concern in South Sudan, with 8,100 infections in 2023 alone and a total of 140,000 people living with the disease; said the enforcement of prevention measures slowed down by limited funding and emphasized awareness campaigns to sensitize populations about the importance and treatment of the virus; according to the vice president, various assessments indicated that several challenges are limiting progress in HIV prevention including underfunding of HIV prevention programs and dependency on external support.

a6346.speaker: Awel, Minister of Health of South Sudan
a6346.name: Awel
a6346.title: Minister of Health of South Sudan
a6346.speech: Has also expressed dismay over the limited funding allocated to the health sector in the annual fiscal year budget, adding that the underfunding frustrates reforms implementation in the health system; she underscored that the government allocated only 1.3 percent of the 4.2 trillion-pound fiscal year budget to the health sector, which is less than the 2% allocated in the 2023-2024 and will only cater for salaries and incentives of health workers.

a6346.speaker: Health Pooled Fund
a6346.name: Health Pooled Fund
a6346.speech: According to Health Pooled Fund, access to healthcare service remains a challenge for many communities in South Sudan, and even reaching a health facility does not guarantee access to appropriate care.

a6371.speaker: UN World Health Organization (WHO)
a6371.name: UN World Health Organization (WHO)
a6371.speech: Said eight countries - six of them in Africa, including Nigeria, Kenya and Lesotho - could soon run out of HIV drugs following the US government's recent decision to pause foreign aid.

a6371.speaker: Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, WHO chief
a6371.name: Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus
a6371.title: WHO chief
a6371.speech: Warned "Disruptions to HIV programmes could undo 20 years of progress" ; added it could also lead to more than 10 million additional cases of HIV and three million HIV-related deaths, noting this was "more than triple the number of deaths last year".

a6371.speaker: Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, WHO chief
a6371.name: Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus
a6371.title: WHO chief
a6371.speech: Said at a press conference on Monday that Nigeria, Kenya, Lesotho, South Sudan, Burkina Faso and Mali - as well as Haiti and Ukraine - would run out of life-saving anti-retroviral (ARV) medicines in the coming months.

a6371.speaker: Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, WHO chief
a6371.name: Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus
a6371.title: WHO chief
a6371.speech: Said the aid pause has led to the "immediate stop to services for HIV treatment, testing and prevention in more than 50 countries".

a6371.speaker: Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, WHO chief
a6371.name: Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus
a6371.title: WHO chief
a6371.speech: "The US administration has been extremely generous over many years. And of course, it's within its rights to decide what it supports and to what extent" ; "But the US also has a responsibility to ensure that if it withdraws direct funding for countries, it's done in an orderly and humane way that allows them to find alternative sources of funding." ; "We ask the US to reconsider its support for global health, which not only saves lives around the world, it also makes the US safer by preventing outbreaks from spreading internationally."

a6371.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a6371.name: Donald Trump
a6371.title: US President
a6371.speech: Announced the freeze on foreign aid on his first day in office in January as part of a review into government spending, pausing foreign aid support for an initial duration of 90 days in line with his "America First" foreign policy.
