a6371.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a6371.name: Donald Trump
a6371.title: US President
a6371.speech: Announced during his first days in office that the US would pull out of the WHO, affecting funding for the global health agency.

a6371.speaker: WHO data
a6371.name: WHO data
a6371.speech: Kenya has the seventh-largest number of people living with HIV in the world, at around 1.4 million, according to WHO data.

a6413.speaker: International Monetary Fund (IMF)
a6413.name: International Monetary Fund (IMF)
a6413.speech: The IMF cite lack of fiscal discipline as one of the reasons that the Extended Credit Facility arrangement had to be cancelled.

a6413.speaker: Malawi's leaders / Tonse Alliance administration
a6413.name: Malawi's leaders / Tonse Alliance administration
a6413.speech: When things started going South soon after they got into government in 2021, our leaders tried so hard to make us believe that it was the Covid-19 pandemic that had disturbed their otherwise perfect plan to economic progress; when years drifted by and Covid was no longer an issue, they came back to the podium with a new narrative that would justify their failure - the Ukraine war.

a6413.speaker: Malawi government / Tonse Alliance administration
a6413.name: Malawi government / Tonse Alliance administration
a6413.speech: In the recent crisis, they claim that their failure to meet the conditions of the ECF can be attributed to exogenous factors - meaning things outside their control.

a6518.speaker: Donald Trump administration
a6518.name: Donald Trump administration
a6518.speech: Announced on Wednesday 26 February 2025 massive budget cuts in American development and foreign aid programmes, eliminating more than 90% of public funding abroad and intending thereby to put an end to the budget of USAID, the United States Agency for International Development.

a6518.speaker: Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE), United States (social media publication)
a6518.name: Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE)
a6518.title: United States (social media publication)
a6518.speech: In a publication on social media on 15 February 2025, cited Mali among the countries whose American grants have been cancelled, mentioning a supposed grant to Mali of 14 million US dollars (about eight billion eight hundred million CFA francs) in support of social cohesion.

a6518.speaker: Embassy of the United States in Mali
a6518.name: Embassy of the United States in Mali
a6518.speech: According to the US Embassy in Mali, “this financing will cover new and ongoing activities in the fields of health, governance, agriculture and basic education.” The same source indicates that “the Malian Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation, Abdoulaye Diop, and the director of the United States Agency for International Development (USAID) in Mali, Miriam Lutz, signed an amendment to the development assistance agreement between the United States and Mali, representing new financing of 148.5 million dollars (101 billion CFA francs)” and that “this amount is in addition to the more than 250 million dollars (170 billion CFA francs) that the United States granted to Mali through USAID over the past year, including 90 million dollars (61 billion CFA francs) in life-saving humanitarian aid for the Malians who need it most.” The American side justified this aid by affirming that the signing of development assistance agreements “represents the unwavering commitment of the United States in favour of a more peaceful and more prosperous Mali that leads its own development,” and that “this new financing for Mali would directly enable 300,000 farming families to benefit from fertiliser and improved seeds in order to strengthen the country's capacity to feed its population without having to depend on costly imports,” with “part of this aid already visible on the ground with USAID's distribution of 1.2 million 500g bags of enriched flour to more than five thousand pregnant and breastfeeding women and 30,000 young children.”

a6518.speaker: Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation of Mali (MAECI, communiqué)
a6518.name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation of Mali (MAECI
a6518.title: communiqué)
a6518.speech: Deemed it necessary to provide clarifications, saying it followed with surprise the publication by the United States Department of Government Efficiency on 15 February 2025 citing Mali among the countries whose American grants have been cancelled, and informing that it has officially approached the American authorities on this subject.

a6518.speaker: Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation of Mali (MAECI, communiqué)
a6518.name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation of Mali (MAECI
a6518.title: communiqué)
a6518.speech: Recalled that Mali, in its quest for sovereignty, has never ceased to denounce, well before the installation of the new American administration, the danger of the diverted use of “public development aid” as an instrument of destabilisation and subversion of our countries through the financing of terrorist networks and as a means of violating the sovereignty of our States ; specified that the Government of Mali has for two years refrained from signing the five-year Development Objective Grant Agreement with the United States for the financing of projects initiated and steered by USAID, and has postponed the implementation of certain activities ; indicated that Mali has placed all of its cooperation relations within the framework of respect for the sovereignty of the State, the sovereign choices of the Malian People and the defence of its interests, including those relating to social cohesion, on condition of respecting Mali's sovereignty, national priorities and implementation procedures.

a6518.speaker: Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation of Mali (MAECI, communiqué)
a6518.name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation of Mali (MAECI
a6518.title: communiqué)
a6518.speech: In line with the vision of the President of the Transition, Head of State, Mali says it recognises the new orientation of the American authorities aimed at cleaning up and humanising their grants, and welcomes this awareness of the reality of their “public aid” and the actions undertaken against its subversive use not conforming to the essential needs of the beneficiaries ; reaffirms that Mali's Transition Authorities will continue their efforts of securing the country, restoring peace, social cohesion and sustainable development, in a dynamic of national ownership, partnership and mutual respect and within the framework of the Confederation of Sahel States ; invites the American authorities to bring judicial proceedings against the persons who diverted the said funds to finance international terrorism, of which Mali and the other States of the AES Confederation are victims.

a6756.speaker: Ambassador Mamman Nuhu, Executive Secretary of the Lake Chad Basin Commission and Head of Mission of the Multinational Joint Task Force
a6756.name: Ambassador Mamman Nuhu
a6756.title: Executive Secretary of the Lake Chad Basin Commission and Head of Mission of the Multinational Joint Task Force
a6756.speech: On environmental challenges: "We are losing a lot of plant life and animals, including fish species. Farmers, herders and fishermen have lost their livelihoods. It's a real crisis for us."

a6756.speaker: Ambassador Mamman Nuhu, Executive Secretary of the Lake Chad Basin Commission and Head of Mission of the Multinational Joint Task Force
a6756.name: Ambassador Mamman Nuhu
a6756.title: Executive Secretary of the Lake Chad Basin Commission and Head of Mission of the Multinational Joint Task Force
a6756.speech: On defeating Boko Haram: "We have made progress. Some territories have been recovered, and now Boko Haram is only in a few places around Lake Chad, but it still has capacity to cause harm. What we need to do as the Multinational Joint Task Force [MJTF], which we are already doing and seeing good results, is to have continuous military operations. Previously, we had operations for a limited period and then there was a lull."

a6756.speaker: Ambassador Mamman Nuhu, Executive Secretary of the Lake Chad Basin Commission and Head of Mission of the Multinational Joint Task Force
a6756.name: Ambassador Mamman Nuhu
a6756.title: Executive Secretary of the Lake Chad Basin Commission and Head of Mission of the Multinational Joint Task Force
a6756.speech: On progress addressing humanitarian challenges: "The humanitarian challenges are still there. About 10.7 million people need humanitarian assistance. Another 2.4 million people are displaced and are yet to return to their hometowns and villages. We have made some progress. Some of the displaced people in neighbouring countries are returning voluntarily, and we are reintegrating them into their communities. A lot of reconstruction is going on-schools and marketplaces are being rebuilt, and civil authorities are gradually going back to the places that are safe."

a6756.speaker: Ambassador Mamman Nuhu, Executive Secretary of the Lake Chad Basin Commission and Head of Mission of the Multinational Joint Task Force
a6756.name: Ambassador Mamman Nuhu
a6756.title: Executive Secretary of the Lake Chad Basin Commission and Head of Mission of the Multinational Joint Task Force
a6756.speech: On the regional strategy: "We have a robust regional stabilisation strategy crafted in 2018 by the Lake Chad Basin Commission, with the assistance of the African Union and the UN Development Programme [UNDP]. It is an all-encompassing approach with nine pillars, including education and skills acquisition, socio-economic recovery, environmental sustainability, and empowerment and inclusion of women. These are the robust ways we will address some of the regional issues in a non-violent way. The regional stabilisation strategy has not yet fully come on stream. In 2019 a UNDP facility helped raise $60 million, which is what we are currently using to address some of the humanitarian challenges."

a6756.speaker: Ambassador Mamman Nuhu, Executive Secretary of the Lake Chad Basin Commission and Head of Mission of the Multinational Joint Task Force
a6756.name: Ambassador Mamman Nuhu
a6756.title: Executive Secretary of the Lake Chad Basin Commission and Head of Mission of the Multinational Joint Task Force
a6756.speech: On the African Union's "Silencing the Guns by 2020" campaign: "It will take sustained pressure on Boko Haram, along with interventions that address the root causes of the problems in the Lake Chad Basin. For example, poverty and hunger are caused by drought and the shrinking of the lake. If we address the developmental issues, we will be able to silence the guns. Imagine: in the 1960s, the lake occupied 25,000 square kilometers; currently, it is 4,500 square kilometers. Over the same period, the population increased from 7 million to about 50 million."

a6756.speaker: Ambassador Mamman Nuhu, Executive Secretary of the Lake Chad Basin Commission and Head of Mission of the Multinational Joint Task Force
a6756.name: Ambassador Mamman Nuhu
a6756.title: Executive Secretary of the Lake Chad Basin Commission and Head of Mission of the Multinational Joint Task Force
a6756.speech: On efforts underway: "We are addressing the human aspects such as unsustainable methods of farming, which consume a lot of water. We are introducing drought-resistant crops and new farming techniques to enable farmers to use water more efficiently. There is also a sensitisation campaign to educate people on sustainable ways of farming."

a6756.speaker: Ambassador Mamman Nuhu, Executive Secretary of the Lake Chad Basin Commission and Head of Mission of the Multinational Joint Task Force
a6756.name: Ambassador Mamman Nuhu
a6756.title: Executive Secretary of the Lake Chad Basin Commission and Head of Mission of the Multinational Joint Task Force
a6756.speech: Final message: "The cordial relationship among countries of the Lake Chad region should continue. We also need the support of the international community so that we can mobilise the needed funding for these interventions. The countries of the region are not in a financial position to handle these huge projects on their own."

a6805.speaker: One humanitarian worker in Myanmar (anonymous)
a6805.name: One humanitarian worker in Myanmar (anonymous)
a6805.speech: described the situation as “mayhem.”

a6805.speaker: Dozens of aid workers and UN staff (anonymous)
a6805.name: Dozens of aid workers and UN staff (anonymous)
a6805.speech: told Reuters that nearly three weeks into US President Donald Trump's sweeping freeze on foreign aid, life-saving programmes across the globe remain shut as humanitarian workers struggle to secure US government waivers meant to keep them open.

a6805.speaker: Marco Rubio, US Secretary of State
a6805.name: Marco Rubio
a6805.title: US Secretary of State
a6805.speech: issued waivers for what he called “life-saving humanitarian assistance,” which included “core life-saving medicine, medical services, food, shelter, and subsistence assistance.”

a6805.speaker: Aid workers and UN officials (anonymous)
a6805.name: Aid workers and UN officials (anonymous)
a6805.speech: said the waivers had sparked widespread confusion, along with fears that their US funding would never be restored ; They said they couldn’t restart work without first confirming with their US counterparts whether specific programmes qualified for exemption. This was proving nearly impossible, they said, due to a communication breakdown with US officials, some of whom had been fired or barred from talking ; Aid workers said their organisations erred on the side of caution and closed programmes rather than incur expenses that the US government might not reimburse. Some described how US partners – often people they had worked with for years – no longer answered their phones or emails.

a6805.speaker: Recording of a 31 January USAID staff meeting (reviewed by Reuters)
a6805.name: Recording of a 31 January USAID staff meeting (reviewed by Reuters)
a6805.speech: According to a previously unreported recording of the meeting reviewed by Reuters, staff at the United States Agency for International Development were told not to communicate externally about the waiver and what it may or may not include.

a6805.speaker: US State Department and White House
a6805.name: US State Department and White House
a6805.speech: did not respond to requests for comment.

a6805.speaker: One Geneva-based aid official (anonymous)
a6805.name: One Geneva-based aid official (anonymous)
a6805.speech: “We asked: Can you tell us exactly which programmes we need to stop? Then we got a message saying ‘no more guidance is forthcoming’. This leaves us in a situation where you have to make a choice of which programme is ‘life-saving’,” the official said. “We don’t have money to pay for it ourselves. We can’t spend money we don’t know if we have.”

a6805.speaker: Elon Musk, Trump’s government efficiency tsar
a6805.name: Elon Musk
a6805.title: Trump’s government efficiency tsar
a6805.speech: targeted USAID for closure as a “criminal organisation.”

a6805.speaker: Donald Trump, US President (executive order)
a6805.name: Donald Trump
a6805.title: US President (executive order)
a6805.speech: In his executive order, Trump said the US “foreign aid industry and bureaucracy” were “in many cases antithetical to American values.” He ordered the 90-day pause pending a review on whether aid was consistent with his “America First” foreign policy.

a6805.speaker: Two workers with aid organisations in Myanmar (anonymous)
a6805.name: Two workers with aid organisations in Myanmar (anonymous)
a6805.speech: told Reuters they didn’t know whether US-funded food distribution in the country was covered by a waiver and would continue. One of the workers described the situation as “mayhem.”

a6805.speaker: UN
a6805.name: UN
a6805.speech: An estimated two million people in the country are on the brink of famine, according to the UN.

a6805.speaker: Inter Sector Coordination Group (draft statement to local aid groups)
a6805.name: Inter Sector Coordination Group (draft statement to local aid groups)
a6805.speech: “Some essential and life-saving services” had been interrupted by the freeze, said the Inter Sector Coordination Group, an international relief organisation that oversees the camps, in a previously unreported draft statement to local aid groups. The group didn’t respond to a request for comment.

a6805.speaker: A UN official in Bangladesh (anonymous)
a6805.name: A UN official in Bangladesh (anonymous)
a6805.speech: seeking clarity on which programmes could remain open said US counterparts were “not answering the phones.”

a6805.speaker: A USAID contractor (anonymous)
a6805.name: A USAID contractor (anonymous)
a6805.speech: said humanitarian workers were due to start anti-malaria spraying campaigns this month in Ghana and Kenya before mosquito populations explode during the rainy season, but insecticide and mosquito nets are stuck in warehouses ; said campaigns to protect millions of people appeared on hold as aid workers sought clarification on when funding would resume and specific malaria programmes in Africa could restart ; “There is a small window to do those campaigns which is going to close rapidly.”

a6805.speaker: USAID memo dated 4 February (seen by Reuters)
a6805.name: USAID memo dated 4 February (seen by Reuters)
a6805.speech: said “life-saving activities” to address malaria, tuberculosis and other diseases and conditions would be exempt from the freeze.

a6805.speaker: World Health Organization
a6805.name: World Health Organization
a6805.speech: The vast majority of the world’s 597 000 malaria deaths in 2023 were African children aged under five years old, the World Health Organization said in December.

a6805.speaker: Malaria No More
a6805.name: Malaria No More
a6805.speech: said the freeze could prevent the distribution of 15.6 million life-saving treatments, nine million nets and 48 million doses of preventative medicine.

a6805.speaker: President's Malaria Initiative (PMI) website statement
a6805.name: President's Malaria Initiative (PMI) website statement
a6805.speech: “In order to be consistent with the President's Executive Orders, this website is currently undergoing maintenance as we expeditiously and thoroughly review all of the content.”

a6805.speaker: Anne Linn, USAID staffer (technical advisor, fired 28 January)
a6805.name: Anne Linn
a6805.title: USAID staffer (technical advisor, fired 28 January)
a6805.speech: “It’s as if all the work . . . has just been erased,” said Anne Linn. “It’s so cruel and senseless,” she said. “The wastefulness of it is staggering to me.”

a6805.speaker: An aid worker (anonymous, on the International Rescue Committee)
a6805.name: An aid worker (anonymous
a6805.title: on the International Rescue Committee)
a6805.speech: said IRC was told by US officials they couldn’t reopen before receiving another notification, which hasn’t arrived.

a6805.speaker: Francois Nosten, director of the Shoklo Malaria Research Unit
a6805.name: Francois Nosten
a6805.title: director of the Shoklo Malaria Research Unit
a6805.speech: said many were discharged from the IRC facilities, leaving people including pregnant women and children unable to access medication or medical equipment ; If “you cut all the activities then some people are going to die.”

a6805.speaker: Family of an elderly woman discharged from an IRC facility
a6805.name: Family of an elderly woman discharged from an IRC facility
a6805.speech: According to her family, an elderly woman, who had been hospitalised with lung problems and was dependent on oxygen, died four days after being discharged.

a6805.speaker: IRC spokesperson
a6805.name: IRC spokesperson
a6805.speech: said some refugees had “self-organised” to provide critical services for themselves until aid support was “transitioned” to Thai authorities.

a6805.speaker: Aid workers (anonymous)
a6805.name: Aid workers (anonymous)
a6805.speech: said millions of US taxpayer dollars already spent on supplies to fight malaria in Africa could go to waste.

a6822.speaker: World Food Programme (WFP)
a6822.name: World Food Programme (WFP)
a6822.speech: Warned on Tuesday that millions of people risk suffering from hunger as southern Africa enters the lean season, and issued an appeal for urgent aid in southern Africa to prevent the widespread drought triggered by El Nino from turning into a “real humanitarian catastrophe.” According to the UN agency, five southern African countries — Lesotho, Malawi, Namibia, Zambia and Zimbabwe — have all declared the hunger crisis a disaster, requesting international humanitarian assistance, while Angola and Mozambique are also severely affected.

a6822.speaker: World Food Programme (WFP)
a6822.name: World Food Programme (WFP)
a6822.speech: According to WFP, harvests have not met farmers’ expectations, livestock has perished and children are lucky to receive even one meal a day; the region faces a “historic” drought threatening more than 27 million lives, while around 21 million children suffer from malnutrition, and for many communities this is the “worst food crisis in decades.”

a6822.speaker: World Food Programme (WFP)
a6822.name: World Food Programme (WFP)
a6822.speech: Says that, at the request of governments, it has begun providing food aid and essential support in transport, logistics and food procurement, and that it plans to scale up seasonal relief operations in the coming months and distribute food and cash in certain regions to more than 6.5 million people in the seven hardest-hit countries until March 2025.

a6822.speaker: Tomson Phiri, WFP spokesperson for southern Africa
a6822.name: Tomson Phiri
a6822.title: WFP spokesperson for southern Africa
a6822.speech: “The month of October marks the beginning of the lean season and each month is expected to be worse than the previous one until the next harvests in March/April” ; “The situation is dire and the need to act has never been more evident,” stressing that more than 6.5 million people need assistance in these seven countries.

a6822.speaker: Tomson Phiri, WFP spokesperson for southern Africa
a6822.name: Tomson Phiri
a6822.title: WFP spokesperson for southern Africa
a6822.speech: Warned: “If we do not receive additional resources, millions of people risk going through the worst lean season known in decades without receiving any aid,” calling for massive funding to carry out the planned actions.

a6922.speaker: Sources
a6922.name: Sources
a6922.speech: Said Prince Daron Obasa, the businessman who facilitated the deal, secured a loan from the Nigerian bank using a Ghana Army guarantee.

a6922.speaker: Top Ghana Army officer (unnamed)
a6922.name: Top Ghana Army officer (unnamed)
a6922.speech: Said he was using the money to look after the children of the late businessman, Prince Darron Obasa, who died in 2021.

a6922.speaker: Reports
a6922.name: Reports
a6922.speech: Indicate that Col. Michael Nkrumah, the then Service Financial Controller for the Ghana Army, allegedly facilitated the cash transaction without the knowledge or authorization of General Oppong-Peprah, the Chief of Army Staff.

a6922.speaker: Colonel Awuah Ameyaw, Deputy Director of Army Legal Affairs
a6922.name: Colonel Awuah Ameyaw
a6922.title: Deputy Director of Army Legal Affairs
a6922.speech: Is said to vigorously defend the Army's position, though many remain skeptical about its credibility.

a6922.speaker: Insiders
a6922.name: Insiders
a6922.speech: Reveal that the matter has been discussed at the highest levels of the Ghana Armed Forces (GAF), but no decisive action has been taken against those involved ; indicate that while it is common practice for the GAF to loan pistols and other weapons to the National Security Secretariat for operations and training, Lt General Onwona's handling of this particular ammunition transfer has been called into question.

a6922.speaker: The Herald (newspaper's own reporting)
a6922.name: The Herald (newspaper's own reporting)
a6922.speech: Has learned that Col. Nkrumah had previously disclosed details of the US$250,000 transaction to former military heads, including the then-Chief of the Defence Staff (CDS), Vice Admiral Seth Amoama, currently Ghana's High Commissioner to Nigeria, but no formal action was taken at the time.

a6922.speaker: Military sources
a6922.name: Military sources
a6922.speech: Said the Board of Inquiry is led by Vice Admiral Issah Adam Yakubu, the Chief of Naval Staff, with Brigadier General Winfred Dzandu-Hedidor, the Director General in Charge of GAF, also serving as a member.

a6922.speaker: General Thomas Oppong-Peprah, Chief of Defence Staff
a6922.name: General Thomas Oppong-Peprah
a6922.title: Chief of Defence Staff
a6922.speech: Alleges that the missing ammunition transfer could be used to topple the Mahama government.

a6922.speaker: Some sources
a6922.name: Some sources
a6922.speech: Argue that General Oppong-Peprah himself engaged in similar, if not worse, practices when he served as Army Commander.

a6922.speaker: Reports
a6922.name: Reports
a6922.speech: Suggest that Major General William Azure Ayamdo, a retired Army Commander, could be cited as a witness to such precedents.

a6922.speaker: Sources
a6922.name: Sources
a6922.speech: Indicate that General Oppong-Peprah has recently shifted his political alignments, reconnecting with his Bono regional ties and building relationships with prominent figures in the ruling National Democratic Congress (NDC).

a6922.speaker: Nana Akufo-Addo, former President of Ghana (final State of the Nation Address, January 3, 2025)
a6922.name: Nana Akufo-Addo
a6922.title: former President of Ghana (final State of the Nation Address, January 3, 2025)
a6922.speech: Announced: "In line with our commitment to aligning with international military norms and enhancing the authority of our top military officials, I am pleased, as Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces, to announce the elevation of the Chief of the Defence Staff (CDS) to the rank of General, and the Chiefs of Army Staff, Navy Staff, Air Staff, and the Chief of Staff at the General Headquarters to the rank of Lieutenant General or its equivalent" ; he added: "These promotions, alongside our successes in anti-terrorism programmes and cross-border security initiatives, position Ghana as a serious player in defence, and bolster our international partnerships in peacekeeping and security."

a7061.speaker: JD Vance, US Vice President
a7061.name: JD Vance
a7061.title: US Vice President
a7061.speech: Remarked on retaliation in a legal context against the EU's bid to regulate Artificial Intelligence.

a7061.speaker: Ichikowitz Foundation African Youth Survey 2020
a7061.name: Ichikowitz Foundation African Youth Survey 2020
a7061.speech: Indicates that Africa holds the world's youngest population, with 70% of the youth living in sub-Saharan Africa and under 30 years of age; the same survey projected that by 2050, African youth are expected to account for a third of the world's youth population.

a7061.speaker: Statista
a7061.name: Statista
a7061.speech: As of 2020, Africa had around 1,173 million hectares of agricultural land, which corresponds to 40% of the total land area of the region.

a7061.speaker: The Africa Center for Strategic Studies
a7061.name: The Africa Center for Strategic Studies
a7061.speech: According to the Center, the war [in Sudan] has already led to 6 million cross-border displacement.

a7061.speaker: Survey conducted in 16 African nations
a7061.name: Survey conducted in 16 African nations
a7061.speech: Revealed that nearly 60% of youth want to leave their countries because of unchecked corruption.

a7061.speaker: Jose Ugaz, Transparency International
a7061.name: Jose Ugaz
a7061.title: Transparency International
a7061.speech: According to him, while corrupt individuals with political power enjoy a lavish life, millions of Africans are deprived of their basic needs like food, health, education, housing, access to clean water and sanitation.

a7061.speaker: African Development Bank
a7061.name: African Development Bank
a7061.speech: Highlights that "corruption drains an estimated 10 billion Dollars annually from African economies diverting crucial resources from healthcare education and infrastructure development." This illicit financial flow undermines economic growth and erodes public trust in institutions on the continent.

a7061.speaker: Policy transfer scholars (Dolowitz and Marsh, Stone, Evans and Davies, Ousmane and others)
a7061.name: Policy transfer scholars (Dolowitz and Marsh
a7061.title: Stone, Evans and Davies, Ousmane and others)
a7061.speech: Have all agreed that policy transfer is a way one political setting can learn from the policies, institutions and administrative arrangements of another.

a7177.speaker: Antony J. Blinken, US Secretary of State
a7177.name: Antony J. Blinken
a7177.title: US Secretary of State
a7177.speech: Posted on the social network X: “I met today with my colleague and friend, Moroccan Foreign Minister Bourita, to discuss the strong strategic partnership between the United States and Morocco and the ways in which we can achieve shared security objectives in the region.” In a message published on X, Blinken underlined the importance of this “strong strategic partnership” and of the common security objectives to be achieved in the region.

a7177.speaker: Antony J. Blinken, US Secretary of State
a7177.name: Antony J. Blinken
a7177.title: US Secretary of State
a7177.speech: On Wednesday, stressed the importance of the “crucial voice” of King Mohammed VI in the aspiration to a “more peaceful and more secure” Middle East; during a meeting with Moroccan Foreign Minister Nasser Bourita, Blinken highlighted Morocco’s “leadership” in the humanitarian response in Gaza, as well as its support for stabilisation in the West Bank and for the revitalisation of the Palestinian Authority.

a7177.speaker: Antony J. Blinken, US Secretary of State
a7177.name: Antony J. Blinken
a7177.title: US Secretary of State
a7177.speech: Also “saluted” Morocco’s efforts to resolve the political impasse in Libya and to address instability in the Sahel region.

a7259.speaker: Chief Cyril Allen, Chairman Emeritus of the National Patriotic Party (NPP)
a7259.name: Chief Cyril Allen
a7259.title: Chairman Emeritus of the National Patriotic Party (NPP)
a7259.speech: Advises President Boakai to prioritize leveraging the country's natural resources and fostering local industrial development to boost the economy; in an exclusive mobile interview, emphasizes the need for Liberia to shift from dependency on foreign aid toward establishing factories and processing plants for its abundant natural wealth, including gold, diamonds, timber, and fisheries; urges the government to revisit successful past initiatives like the Lofa and Bong County Agriculture Development Projects, which he recalls created jobs and increased agricultural outputs; highlights Liberia's potential in the fishing industry, given its extensive coastline, and recalls successes of the timber and plywood industry during former President Charles Taylor's administration, advocating for similar sustainable ventures today ; advocates for a shift from reliance on external funding to inward investment in manufacturing and resource processing, which he says could add value locally and create jobs; calls on the government to manage state resources effectively, including establishing processing plants for minerals and timber; underscores the importance of rebuilding and expanding successful sectors like agriculture, fishing, and timber.

a7259.speaker: Chief Cyril Allen, Chairman Emeritus of the National Patriotic Party (NPP)
a7259.name: Chief Cyril Allen
a7259.title: Chairman Emeritus of the National Patriotic Party (NPP)
a7259.speech: Points to internal party dynamics, urging unity among NPP members in Tuesday's Nimba County Senatorial By-election, emphasizing the importance of maintaining party cohesion and preparing for the future, and emphasizes unity and strategic organization within the NPP to strengthen its electoral prospects.

a7442.speaker: John Maynard Keynes (public letter to U.S. President Franklin Delano Roosevelt, end of 1933)
a7442.name: John Maynard Keynes (public letter to U.S. President Franklin Delano Roosevelt
a7442.title: end of 1933)
a7442.speech: Approved of the general direction of FDR's New Deal policies, but also had some sharp criticism. He worried that FDR complicated the economic recovery effort by broadening his policy agenda unnecessarily; that FDR was doing too little to increase aggregate demand and too much to change the rules of the economy. Keynes took particular aim at the National Industrial Recovery Act, fretting that the NIRA would sap business confidence and weigh on the federal bureaucracy, without making a direct contribution to recovery. He wondered whether some of the advice FDR was getting "is not crack-brained and queer."

a7442.speaker: Sebastian Edwards, book 'American Default'
a7442.name: Sebastian Edwards
a7442.title: book 'American Default'
a7442.speech: Explains that the predominant view among economists was that breaking the dollar's link with gold would create havoc and uncertainty.

a7442.speaker: Dani Rodrik (comment author)
a7442.name: Dani Rodrik (comment author)
a7442.speech: Argues that today's problems demand bold responses, yet mainstream economists seem preoccupied with marginal fixes that leave untouched the structures of power underwriting the rules of the economic game; says economists can rise to the challenge by adopting a broader vision, and that he joined a group of prominent economists to launch an initiative called "Economics for Inclusive Prosperity" (EfIP), whose goal is to advance ambitious policy ideas that pay much closer attention to inequality and exclusion - and to the power imbalances that produce them.
